photographers.name: John Thomson

portrait.credit: Fotograf unbekannt, Wellcome Collection (Ausschnitt aus „Two Manchu soldiers with John Thomson“) / CC BY 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: John Thomson | Historic Environment Scotland
sources.excerpt: Born in Edinburgh when photography was in its infancy, Thomson was to become one of its leading innovators. He was known as 'China' Thomson because of the incredible photographs he took when travelling in Asia.

sources.title: John Thomson | Historic Environment Scotland
sources.excerpt: Having become fascinated as a boy with the science behind the new medium, Thomson learned about optics, and therefore how camera lenses work, when apprenticed to an optician. Highly motivated to learn more, he gained a diploma at Edinburgh School of Arts which enabled him to attend Chemistry lectures at the University.

sources.title: John Thomson | Historic Environment Scotland
sources.excerpt: Settling in London, he set about publishing books of his photographs, the most famous of these is 'Illustrations of China and Its People' which was published in 1873. His other major work was 'Street Life in London', 1877; a compelling and sympathetic portraits of the capital's poor which established social documentary photography as a new genre.

sources.title: Icons of Photography - Iconic Photographer John Thomson (1837-1921) | Amateur Photographer
sources.excerpt: Photographing in remote regions at the time was fraught with difficulty. Thomson used the most advanced method available at the time, the wet-plate collodion process, but the large wooden cameras and tripods were cumbersome and the processing chemicals were often hard to find.

sources.title: Icons of Photography - Iconic Photographer John Thomson (1837-1921) | Amateur Photographer
sources.excerpt: John Thomson was an intrepid and determined photographer, whose groundbreaking work documented social conditions both in Britain and the Far East. At different times, he set up commercial portrait studios in London, Singapore and Hong Kong, but his real interest was photographing ordinary people in their daily lives.

photographers.bio_md: John Thomson stammte aus Edinburgh und wurde wegen seiner Aufnahmen aus Asien „China“ Thomson genannt [Q1]. Als Lehrling bei einem Optiker lernte er, wie Kameraobjektive funktionieren, und besuchte nach einem Diplom der Edinburgh School of Arts Chemievorlesungen an der Universität [Q2]. Er betrieb Porträtstudios in London, Singapur und Hongkong, sein eigentliches Interesse galt aber gewöhnlichen Menschen in ihrem Alltag [Q5]. In London veröffentlichte er „Illustrations of China and Its People“ (1873) und „Street Life in London“ (1877); letzteres zeigt die Armen der Hauptstadt mitfühlend und begründete die soziale Dokumentarfotografie als neues Genre [Q3]. Seine Arbeit dokumentierte soziale Verhältnisse sowohl in Großbritannien als auch im Fernen Osten [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Thomson arbeitete im Nasskollodium-Verfahren, dem fortschrittlichsten Verfahren seiner Zeit, mit großen Holzkameras und Stativen, die auf Reisen in entlegene Regionen schwer zu transportieren waren [Q4]. Im Mittelpunkt standen Menschen in ihrem täglichen Leben statt bloßer Ansichten [Q5].

photographers.name: Fan Ho

portrait.credit: Amazsara10 / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: 10 Facts about the Photographer Who Captured 1950s and '60s Hong Kong | M+
sources.excerpt: Fan Ho (American, b. China, 1931-2016) was a photographer, film director, and actor. He spent his early years in Shanghai, where he began taking photographs after receiving his first camera at fourteen.

sources.title: Bio — Fan Ho Photography
sources.excerpt: At the age of 18, he acquired his twin lens Rolleiflex with which he captured all his famous work after he moved to Hong Kong with his parents and continued to purse his love for photography.

sources.title: Bio — Fan Ho Photography
sources.excerpt: Dubbed the "Cartier-Bresson of the East", Fan Ho patiently waited for 'the decisive moment'; very often a collision of the unexpected, framed against a very clever composed background of geometrical construction, patterns and texture. He often created drama and atmosphere with backlit effects or through the combination of smoke and light. His favorite locations were the streets, alleys and markets around dusk or life on the sea.

sources.title: Fan Ho: On the 'Decisive Moment' | M+
sources.excerpt: I always pay attention to the light. I consider photography as the art of light. The light needs to fit my needs, not to mention achieve contrast. So it's important to wait for the right light.

sources.title: Fan Ho: On the 'Decisive Moment' | M+
sources.excerpt: I actually prefer black and white. It's not that I don't take colour photographs, but I've realised one thing. Colours do not fit well in my world. Black and white offers me a distance.

photographers.bio_md: Fan Ho (1931–2016) war Fotograf, Filmregisseur und Schauspieler; er wuchs in Shanghai auf und fotografierte, seit er mit vierzehn seine erste Kamera bekam [Q1]. Mit 18 erwarb er eine zweiäugige Rolleiflex, mit der er nach dem Umzug nach Hongkong alle seine bekannten Bilder machte [Q2]. Man nannte ihn den „Cartier-Bresson des Ostens“; seine bevorzugten Orte waren Straßen, Gassen und Märkte in der Dämmerung oder das Leben auf dem Wasser [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Fan Ho wartete geduldig auf den „entscheidenden Augenblick“ – oft ein unerwartetes Zusammentreffen vor einem geometrisch gebauten Hintergrund aus Mustern und Texturen – und erzeugte Atmosphäre mit Gegenlicht oder mit Rauch und Licht [Q3]. Er verstand Fotografie als Kunst des Lichts und wartete auf das passende Licht und Kontrast [Q4]. Schwarzweiß zog er vor, weil es ihm Distanz zum farbigen wirklichen Leben gibt [Q5].

photographers.name: Luigi Ghirri

sources.title: Kodachrome – Luigi Ghirri | MACK
sources.excerpt: Born in Scandiano in 1943, Luigi Ghirri spent his working life in the Emilia Romagna region, where he produced one of the most open and layered bodies of work in the history of photography. He was published and exhibited extensively both in Italy and internationally and was at the height of his career at the time of his death in 1992.

sources.title: Luigi Ghirri | Matthew Marks Gallery
sources.excerpt: Inspired in part by the Conceptual art of his time, Luigi Ghirri used his camera to examine the relationship between the physical world and the world of images. His subject was the landscape around him, but his photographs are much more than visual documents of 1970s and 1980s Italy. With his uncanny eye for composition, Ghirri searched out chance arrangements in the human-built world, framing them in his camera's viewfinder like found photomontages.

sources.title: Luigi Ghirri | Matthew Marks Gallery
sources.excerpt: He worked in color because, as he put it, "the real world is in color," and he made modestly sized meticulous prints, rarely producing more than one or two from each image. In 1978 he published Kodachrome , a book of his photographs that touches on many of the subjects that defined his career, including windows, billboards, murals, and other sites where, as he put it, "the world of signs merges with the physical world."

sources.title: Kodachrome – Luigi Ghirri | MACK
sources.excerpt: Part amateur photo-album, Ghirri presents his surroundings in tightly cropped images, making photographs of photographs and recording the Italian landscape through it's adverts, postcards, potted plants, walls, windows, and people. His work is deadpan, reflecting a dry wit, and is a continuous engagement with the subject of reality and of landscape as a snapshot of our interaction with the world.

sources.title: Luigi Ghirri | Matthew Marks Gallery
sources.excerpt: Although he exhibited extensively in Italy during his lifetime, it is only since his untimely death that his work has begun to be more widely appreciated. In 2010 Thomas Demand organized the acclaimed exhibition "La Carte d'Après Nature" around Ghirri's photographs, and in 2011 and 2013 Ghirri's work was featured in the Venice Biennale.

photographers.bio_md: Luigi Ghirri, 1943 in Scandiano geboren, arbeitete sein ganzes Berufsleben in der Emilia-Romagna und schuf dort eines der offensten und vielschichtigsten Werke der Fotografiegeschichte; er starb 1992 auf dem Höhepunkt seiner Laufbahn [Q1]. Angeregt auch von der Konzeptkunst seiner Zeit untersuchte er mit der Kamera das Verhältnis zwischen physischer Welt und Bilderwelt; sein Thema war die Landschaft um ihn herum im Italien der 1970er und 1980er Jahre [Q2]. 1978 veröffentlichte er „Kodachrome“, ein Buch zu Fenstern, Plakatwänden, Wandbildern und anderen Orten, an denen „die Welt der Zeichen mit der physischen Welt verschmilzt“ [Q3]. Breitere Anerkennung kam erst nach seinem frühen Tod, etwa mit Thomas Demands Ausstellung „La Carte d'Après Nature“ (2010) und Auftritten auf der Biennale Venedig 2011 und 2013 [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Ghirri suchte zufällige Anordnungen in der vom Menschen gebauten Welt und rahmte sie im Sucher wie gefundene Fotomontagen [Q2]. Er fotografierte in Farbe, weil „die wirkliche Welt farbig ist“, und machte kleine, sorgfältige Abzüge [Q3]. Seine Bilder sind eng beschnitten, fotografieren oft Fotografien (Werbung, Postkarten) und sind trocken-lakonisch im Ton [Q4].

photographers.name: Alex Webb

portrait.credit: John Ramspott / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Alex Webb • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Alex Webb was born in San Francisco, California, in 1952. He became interested in photography during his high school years and attended the Apeiron Workshops in Millerton, New York, in 1972. He majored in history and literature at Harvard University, simultaneously studying photography at the Carpenter Center for the Arts.

sources.title: Alex Webb • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: In 1974, he began working as a professional photojournalist. He joined Magnum Photos as a nominee in 1974, as an associate in 1976, and as a full member in 1979.

sources.title: Alex Webb • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: During the mid-1970s, Webb photographed in the American South, documenting small-town life in black and white. He also began working in the Caribbean and Mexico, which prompted his starting to photograph in color, which he has continued to do to this day. He has published more than 15 photography books, including Hot Light/Half-Made Worlds , Under A Grudging Sun , The Suffering of Light , La Calle , and Dislocations .

sources.title: Alex Webb • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: "I only know how to approach a place by walking. For what does a street photographer do but walk and watch and wait and talk, and then watch and wait some more, trying to remain confident that the unexpected, the unknown, or the secret heart of the known awaits just around the corner." - Alex Webb

sources.title: Alex Webb • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: He won the Leopold Godowsky Color Photography Award in 1988, the Leica Medal of Excellence in 2000 and the David Octavius Hill Award in 2002.

photographers.bio_md: Alex Webb wurde 1952 in San Francisco geboren; er besuchte 1972 die Apeiron Workshops und studierte in Harvard Geschichte und Literatur, parallel Fotografie am Carpenter Center for the Arts [Q1]. Ab 1974 arbeitete er als Fotojournalist und wurde 1979 Vollmitglied von Magnum Photos [Q2]. Mitte der 1970er fotografierte er Kleinstadtleben im amerikanischen Süden in Schwarzweiß; die Arbeit in der Karibik und in Mexiko brachte ihn zur Farbe, bei der er bis heute geblieben ist [Q3]. Zu seinen mehr als 15 Büchern gehören „Hot Light/Half-Made Worlds“, „Under A Grudging Sun“, „The Suffering of Light“ und „La Calle“ [Q3]. Für seine Farbarbeit erhielt er u. a. 1988 den Leopold Godowsky Color Photography Award und 2000 die Leica Medal of Excellence [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Webb nähert sich einem Ort zu Fuß: gehen, schauen, warten, reden – und wieder schauen und warten, im Vertrauen darauf, dass das Unerwartete gleich um die Ecke wartet [Q4]. Seit seiner Arbeit in der Karibik und Mexiko fotografiert er in Farbe [Q3].

photographers.name: Martin Parr

portrait.credit: Raph_PH / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Martin Parr • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Martin Parr was born in 1952 in Epsom, Surrey. He is one of the best-known documentary photographers of his generation. Having published over 100 books of his own and edited another 30 in his lifetime, Parr built a long-lasting legacy.

sources.title: Acclaimed British photographer Martin Parr dies aged 73 | Al Jazeera
sources.excerpt: He launched his career after studying at the University of Manchester, taking black-and-white shots that aped the great masters of the time such as Henri Cartier-Bresson. But he found himself drawn to colour photography, which was becoming the standard form, inspired by the style of amusing seaside postcards and other kitsch items of everyday 1970s Britain.

sources.title: Acclaimed British photographer Martin Parr dies aged 73 | Al Jazeera
sources.excerpt: Parr rose to prominence with his 1980s collection, The Last Resort, which depicted working-class visitors to the seaside town of New Brighton, with highly saturated shots of frazzled beachgoers lit by lurid flash.

sources.title: Martin Parr | KYOTOGRAPHIE 2025
sources.excerpt: Known for his use of garish colours and esoteric composition, he has studied cultural peculiarities around the world from Japan to America, Europe, and his home country of Britain, also making numerous trips to China since 1985. The themes of leisure, consumption and communication have occupied him for much of his career, all of which are explored with a penetrating irony.

sources.title: Acclaimed documentary photographer Martin Parr dies aged 73 | The Irish News (PA)
sources.excerpt: It is with great sadness that we announce that Martin Parr (1952-2025) died yesterday at home in Bristol.

photographers.bio_md: Martin Parr wurde 1952 in Epsom (Surrey) geboren und gilt als einer der bekanntesten Dokumentarfotografen seiner Generation; er veröffentlichte über 100 eigene Bücher [Q1]. Nach dem Studium an der University of Manchester begann er mit Schwarzweißbildern nach dem Vorbild von Meistern wie Cartier-Bresson, wandte sich dann aber der Farbe zu, angeregt von Seebad-Postkarten und Kitsch des britischen Alltags der 1970er [Q2]. Bekannt wurde er mit „The Last Resort“ aus den 1980ern über Arbeiterfamilien im Seebad New Brighton [Q3]. Freizeit, Konsum und Kommunikation beschäftigten ihn während seiner ganzen Laufbahn, weltweit von Japan bis Amerika [Q4]. Parr starb 2025 in Bristol [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Parrs Bilder sind stark gesättigt, die Menschen oft mit grellem Blitz ausgeleuchtet [Q3]. Bekannt ist er für schrille Farben und eigenwillige Komposition; seine Themen behandelt er mit durchdringender Ironie [Q4].

photographers.name: Zhang Kechun

portrait.credit: Porträt des Fotografen, Huxley-Parlour Gallery (Fotograf nicht angegeben); nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: The Yellow River - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: Zhang Kechun was born in 1980 in Sichuan, China, and started painting when he was a child. He studied art and design and worked as a designer in Chengdu before becoming interested in photography. His first series The Yellow River documented the effects of modernisation along the river.

sources.title: The Yellow River - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: The project took him on a journey along the river from the coastal flats of Shandong to the mountains of Qinghai on a fold-up bicycle, all the time carrying with him a large format Linhof camera.

sources.title: The Yellow River - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: Zhang shot on cloudy days and overexposed the photographs to produce a soft, subtle tonal range.

sources.title: Zhang Kechun - Photographer's Biography & Art Works - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: Zhang Kechun's work examines the post-industrial landscape of China. Working with a large-format camera he produces epic vistas that dwell on the significance of the landscape in modern Chinese national identity. In particular, Kechun explores the relationship between the country's cultural heritage and the effects of modernisation.

sources.title: Zhang Kechun - Photographer's Biography & Art Works - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: In 2014, he received the Discovery Award at Les Rencontres d'Arles for The Yellow River , and more recently was awarded first prize in the Still Life category at the 2023 Sony World Photography Awards.

photographers.bio_md: Zhang Kechun wurde 1980 in Sichuan geboren, malte schon als Kind, studierte Kunst und Design und arbeitete als Designer in Chengdu, bevor er zur Fotografie kam [Q1]. Seine erste Serie „The Yellow River“ dokumentiert die Folgen der Modernisierung entlang des Flusses [Q1]. Sein Werk untersucht die postindustrielle Landschaft Chinas und das Verhältnis von kulturellem Erbe und Modernisierung [Q4]. Für „The Yellow River“ erhielt er 2014 den Discovery Award in Arles, 2023 einen ersten Preis (Still Life) bei den Sony World Photography Awards [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Zhang arbeitet mit der Großformatkamera und baut weite, epische Landschaftsbilder [Q4]. Für „The Yellow River“ fuhr er mit einem Faltrad von der Küste Shandongs bis in die Berge Qinghais, stets mit einer Linhof-Großformatkamera [Q2]. Er fotografierte an bewölkten Tagen und belichtete reichlich, um einen weichen, zarten Tonwertumfang zu erhalten [Q3].

photographers.name: Rinko Kawauchi

portrait.credit: Foto: Arnoldas Kubilius (laut Dateiname), via SFMOMA-Künstlerseite; Rechte bei Urheber, nur Ansicht/Link. Zeigt die Künstlerin von hinten.

sources.title: Rinko Kawauchi | Biography
sources.excerpt: Rinko Kawauchi 1972 Born in Shiga 1993 Graduated Seian Women's College (current Seian University of Art and Design) Lives in Chiba

sources.title: Rinko Kawauchi · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: In contrast to photographers working in the dark and frenetic style developed during the Provoke era of the late 1960s and early 1970s, Rinko Kawauchi (b. 1972) has pursued a more restrained and lyrical aesthetic over more than two decades. The most quotidian objects and occurrences are transformed through her lens into sublime images that frequently highlight the ephemeral, fragile, and even sinister nature of everyday life.

sources.title: Rinko Kawauchi · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Kawauchi studied graphic design and photography at Seian University of Art and Design, Otsu, Japan, and worked in the commercial and advertising realms upon graduating in 1993. She shifted her focus to fine art a few years later and quickly gained international recognition-including the prestigious Kimura Ihei Award-after the simultaneous release of a trilogy of photobooks in 2001: Utatane , Hanabi , and Hanako .

sources.title: Rinko Kawauchi · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Almost entirely devoid of text, these volumes rely on the power of the images speaking to one another across the pages to create their narratives. Common scenes such as a curtain blowing out an open window, soap bubbles gathering in a sink drain, or a young child jumping rope seem to reflect a deeply personal and idiosyncratic experience of the world, as well as a dedicated practice of intense looking. The muted color palette in Utatane , which has become the artist's trademark, produces a dreamy and ethereal atmosphere that complements her sparse and mysterious compositions.

sources.title: Rinko Kawauchi · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Her 2013 project Ametsuchi ventures even further into the metaphysical realm. Focusing on a landscape Kawauchi first encountered in a dream, it captures the centuries-old process of noyaki , a yearly controlled burn of Japan's Aso countryside in order to maintain and refresh the grasslands for grazing animals.

photographers.bio_md: Rinko Kawauchi wurde 1972 in Shiga geboren und lebt in Chiba [Q1]. Sie studierte Grafikdesign und Fotografie an der Seian University of Art and Design in Otsu und arbeitete nach dem Abschluss 1993 zunächst in Werbung und kommerzieller Fotografie [Q3]. Mit der gleichzeitig 2001 erschienenen Buch-Trilogie „Utatane“, „Hanabi“ und „Hanako“ wurde sie international bekannt und erhielt u. a. den Kimura-Ihei-Preis [Q3]. Im Gegensatz zum dunklen, hektischen Provoke-Stil verfolgt sie seit über zwei Jahrzehnten eine zurückhaltende, lyrische Ästhetik [Q2]. 2013 folgte „Ametsuchi“ über das jährliche kontrollierte Abbrennen der Graslandschaft in Aso [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Kawauchi verwandelt alltäglichste Dinge in Bilder, die das Flüchtige und Zerbrechliche des Alltags betonen [Q2]. Ihre fast textlosen Bücher erzählen, indem die Bilder über die Seiten hinweg miteinander sprechen; gedämpfte Farben, ihr Markenzeichen, erzeugen eine traumhafte Atmosphäre zu sparsamen Kompositionen – getragen von intensivem Schauen [Q4].

photographers.name: Timothy H. O'Sullivan

portrait.credit: Philp & Solomons / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Timothy H. O'Sullivan | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: Timothy H. O'Sullivan (1840–1882) was a photographer for two of the most ambitious geographical surveys of the nineteenth century.

sources.title: Timothy H. O'Sullivan | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: O'Sullivan began his photography career as an apprentice in Mathew Brady's Fulton Street gallery in New York City and then moved on to the Washington, D.C., branch managed by Alexander Gardner. In 1861, at the age of twenty-one, O'Sullivan joined Brady's team of Civil War photographers.

sources.title: Timothy H. O'Sullivan | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: In 1867 O'Sullivan joined Clarence King's geological survey of the fortieth parallel-the first federal expedition in the West after the Civil War.

sources.title: Timothy H. O'Sullivan | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: O'Sullivan was strongly influenced by King's interest in the arts (he was a member of the Ruskinian group, the Society for the Advancement of Truth in Art), as well as by contemporary science and its attendant controversies. His work for the King survey often functioned as both objective scientific documentation and a personal evocation of the fantastic and beautiful qualities of the western landscape.

sources.title: Timothy H. O'Sullivan | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: Along these journeys, O'Sullivan produced photographs that exhibit a forthright and rigorous style formed in response to the landscapes he encountered. Faced with challenging terrain and lacking previous photographic examples on which to rely, O'Sullivan created a body of work that was without precedent in its visual and emotional complexities.

photographers.bio_md: Timothy H. O'Sullivan (1840–1882) fotografierte für zwei der ehrgeizigsten geografischen Vermessungsexpeditionen des 19. Jahrhunderts [Q1]. Er lernte als Gehilfe in Mathew Bradys Galerie in New York, wechselte dann zu Alexander Gardner in Washington und gehörte ab 1861 zu Bradys Fotografen im Bürgerkrieg [Q2]. 1867 schloss er sich Clarence Kings Vermessung des 40. Breitengrades an, der ersten Bundesexpedition in den Westen nach dem Krieg [Q3]. Kings Interesse an Kunst und Wissenschaft prägte ihn; seine Bilder waren zugleich wissenschaftliche Dokumentation und persönliche Beschwörung der fantastischen Schönheit der westlichen Landschaft [Q4].
photographers.method_md: O'Sullivan entwickelte im Gelände einen direkten, strengen Stil als Antwort auf die Landschaften selbst – ohne fotografische Vorbilder, auf die er sich hätte stützen können [Q5]. Seine Aufnahmen verbinden sachliche Dokumentation mit einer persönlichen, fast fantastischen Sicht [Q4].

photographers.name: Carleton E. Watkins

portrait.credit: Carleton E. Watkins / CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Carleton E. Watkins | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: Carleton E. Watkins born Oneonta, NY 1829-died Imola, CA 1916

sources.title: Carleton E. Watkins · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: In the boomtown of San Francisco, he fell into photography by chance when asked by a local daguerreotypist to stand in for a missing employee. A natural adept, he soon established his own business fabricating outdoor photographs for land-dispute cases and mining interests.

sources.title: Carleton E. Watkins | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: He made his first trip to Yosemite in the fall of 1861, producing thirty mammoth-plate and one hundred stereoscopic negatives. They were among the first photographs of the valley sent back east. It was partly based on this material that President Lincoln signed a bill in 1864 banning development in the valley, which led to the establishment of the national-parks system.

sources.title: Carleton E. Watkins · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Carleton Watkins was interested in finding a way to convey the scale of the Western landscape to his audience, much of whom was on the East Coast. And so he had a cabinetmaker build him a giant camera that was capable of producing glass-plate negatives that were 18 by 22 inches.

sources.title: Carleton E. Watkins · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: In wide-ranging travels across the length and breadth of the frontier West, Watkins energetically balanced a practical need to characterize the land before him with his craftsman's pride in a picture plumbed and mitred to perfection.

photographers.bio_md: Carleton E. Watkins wurde 1829 in Oneonta (New York) geboren und starb 1916 in Imola (Kalifornien) [Q1]. Im San Francisco des Goldrauschs kam er zufällig zur Fotografie, als ein Daguerreotypist ihn als Aushilfe einsetzte; bald machte er Außenaufnahmen für Landstreitigkeiten und Bergbaufirmen [Q2]. 1861 reiste er erstmals ins Yosemite-Tal und brachte Mammutplatten- und Stereonegative mit – mit unter den ersten Bildern des Tals im Osten; auch auf ihrer Grundlage unterzeichnete Lincoln 1864 das Gesetz zum Schutz des Tals [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Um die Größe der westlichen Landschaft zu vermitteln, ließ Watkins eine Riesenkamera für Glasnegative von 18 × 22 Zoll bauen [Q4]. Er verband den praktischen Auftrag, das Land zu beschreiben, mit handwerklichem Stolz auf ein bis ins Letzte austariertes Bild [Q5].

photographers.name: Samuel Bourne

portrait.credit: Samuel Bourne / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Samuel Bourne | Alkazi Foundation
sources.excerpt: SAMUEL BOURNE (1834 – 1912) It was the love of photography and an enduring romance with the idea of the 'picturesque' that drove Samuel Bourne to relinquish his post of a bank clerk in Nottingham and travel across continents to India, a land that he knew of only through 'views' produced by the likes of William Hodges and Thomas and William Daniell.

sources.title: Samuel Bourne | Alkazi Foundation
sources.excerpt: Initially disappointed by Calcutta, he quickly reached Simla, where he set up his studio in partnership with a Mr. Howard, as 'Howard & Bourne'. Later the same year, Charles Shepherd, of the firm Shepherd & Robertson, arrived in Simla and joined the partnership, creating Howard, Bourne & Shepherd. By 1865, the business had become Bourne & Shepherd.

sources.title: Samuel Bourne | Alkazi Foundation
sources.excerpt: Bourne is particularly known for the three expeditions he undertook in the Himalayas. In keeping with his love of the 'picturesque' and 'sublime', Samuel Bourne achieved his greatest success and distinction as a photographer through the images he composed in the course of these three known and celebrated journeys.

sources.title: View taken from above the Nithal | Bourne, Samuel | V&A Explore The Collections
sources.excerpt: Bourne writes about the difficulty of photographing this landscape: 'In taking views of snow, unless you get broad masses of it well lit up by the sun, it does not "come out" in the photograph with that purity which conveys the impression of snow.

sources.title: Samuel Bourne | Alkazi Foundation
sources.excerpt: In 1870, Bourne left India to settle in Nottingham, where he built up a highly successful cotton doubling business. He continued to photograph as an amateur, producing views of his travels in the south of France. Samuel Bourne passed away on April 12th, 1912.

photographers.bio_md: Samuel Bourne (1834–1912) gab seine Stelle als Bankangestellter in Nottingham auf, getrieben von der Liebe zur Fotografie und zum „Pittoresken“, und reiste nach Indien, das er nur aus gemalten „Ansichten“ kannte [Q1]. In Simla gründete er ein Studio, aus dem bis 1865 die Firma Bourne & Shepherd wurde [Q2]. Bekannt ist er vor allem für drei Expeditionen in den Himalaya, auf denen er im Geist des Pittoresken und Erhabenen seine wichtigsten Bilder machte [Q3]. 1870 ließ er sich wieder in Nottingham nieder, baute ein Textilgeschäft auf und fotografierte nur noch als Amateur; er starb 1912 [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Bourne komponierte nach den Idealen des Pittoresken und Erhabenen [Q3]. Für Schnee suchte er große, voll von der Sonne beleuchtete Flächen, weil Schnee sonst im Bild nicht rein genug wirke [Q4].

photographers.name: Ansel Adams

portrait.credit: J. Malcolm Greany / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Ansel Adams Biography (American National Biography, Oxford University Press) | anseladams.com
sources.excerpt: Adams, Ansel (Feb. 20 1902 - Apr. 22, 1984), photographer and environmentalist, was born in San Francisco, California, the son of Charles Hitchcock Adams, a businessman, and Olive Bray.

sources.title: Ansel Adams Biography (American National Biography, Oxford University Press) | anseladams.com
sources.excerpt: For the next dozen years the piano was Adams's primary occupation and, by 1920, his intended profession. Although he ultimately gave up music for photography, the piano brought substance, discipline, and structure to his frustrating and erratic youth. Moreover, the careful training and exacting craft required of a musician profoundly informed his visual artistry, as well as his influential writings and teachings on photography.

sources.title: Ansel Adams Biography (American National Biography, Oxford University Press) | anseladams.com
sources.excerpt: The renowned Group f/64, founded in 1932, coalesced around the recognized greatness of Weston and the dynamic energy of Adams. Although loosely organized and relatively short-lived, Group f/64 brought the new West Coast vision of straight photography to national attention and influence.

sources.title: Ansel Adams Biography (American National Biography, Oxford University Press) | anseladams.com
sources.excerpt: Adams developed the famous and highly complex "zone system" of controlling and relating exposure and development, enabling photographers to creatively visualize an image and produce a photograph that matched and expressed that visualization. He produced ten volumes of technical manuals on photography, which are the most influential books ever written on the subject.

sources.title: Ansel Adams Biography (American National Biography, Oxford University Press) | anseladams.com
sources.excerpt: His black-and-white images were not "realistic" documents of nature. Instead, they sought an intensification and purification of the psychological experience of natural beauty. He created a sense of the sublime magnificence of nature that infused the viewer with the emotional equivalent of wilderness, often more powerful than the actual thing.

photographers.bio_md: Ansel Adams (20. Februar 1902 – 22. April 1984), Fotograf und Umweltschützer, wurde in San Francisco geboren [Q1]. Bis etwa 1920 wollte er Pianist werden; die genaue Ausbildung und das handwerkliche Ethos des Musikers prägten später seine Bildsprache und seine einflussreichen Lehrschriften [Q2]. Um Edward Weston und ihn formierte sich 1932 die Group f/64, die die „straight photography“ der Westküste landesweit bekannt machte [Q3]. Er entwickelte das „Zonensystem“ und schrieb zehn Bände technischer Handbücher, die als die einflussreichsten Bücher zu diesem Thema gelten [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Mit dem Zonensystem stimmte Adams Belichtung und Entwicklung so aufeinander ab, dass das fertige Bild der vorher „visualisierten“ Vorstellung entsprach [Q4]. Seine Schwarzweißbilder wollten keine realistischen Dokumente sein, sondern das Erleben von Naturschönheit verdichten und läutern – ein Gefühl des Erhabenen, oft stärker als der Ort selbst [Q5].

photographers.name: Henri Cartier-Bresson

portrait.credit: Ihei Kimura / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Biography - Fondation Henri Cartier-Bresson
sources.excerpt: 1908: Born on August 22nd in Chanteloup, Seine-et-Marne. Educated at the Lycée Condorcet, Paris. 1926: Studies painting under André Lhote. Takes his first photographs.

sources.title: Biography - Fondation Henri Cartier-Bresson
sources.excerpt: 1947: Exhibition Photographs by Henri Cartier-Bresson at the Museum of Modern Art in New York. Creates the cooperative agency Magnum Photos with Robert Capa, David Seymour (Chim), William Vandivert, and George Rodger.

sources.title: Henri Cartier-Bresson | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: His photographs may be summed up through a phrase of his own: "the decisive moment," the magical instant when the world falls into apparent order and meaning, and may be apprehended by a gifted photographer.

sources.title: Henri Cartier-Bresson - Fondation Henri Cartier-Bresson
sources.excerpt: For me the camera is a sketch book, an instrument of intuition and spontaneity, the master of the instant which, in visual terms, questions and decides simultaneously. In order to give a "meaning" to the world, one has to feel involved in what one frames through the viewfinder. This attitude requires concentration, discipline of mind, sensitivity, and a sense of geometry.

sources.title: Biography - Fondation Henri Cartier-Bresson
sources.excerpt: 1974: Terminates his active working relationship with Magnum Photos, although the agency distribution retains his archives. Concentrates on drawing.

photographers.bio_md: Henri Cartier-Bresson wurde am 22. August 1908 in Chanteloup (Seine-et-Marne) geboren, besuchte das Lycée Condorcet in Paris und studierte ab 1926 Malerei bei André Lhote, als er auch die ersten Fotos machte [Q1]. 1947 zeigte das Museum of Modern Art seine Fotografien, im selben Jahr gründete er mit Robert Capa, David Seymour, William Vandivert und George Rodger die Kooperative Magnum Photos [Q2]. Seine Bilder lassen sich mit seinem eigenen Begriff zusammenfassen: dem „entscheidenden Augenblick“, in dem die Welt in scheinbare Ordnung und Bedeutung fällt [Q3]. 1974 beendete er die aktive Arbeit für Magnum und konzentrierte sich aufs Zeichnen [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Für Cartier-Bresson war die Kamera ein Skizzenbuch, ein Instrument der Intuition und Spontaneität; wer der Welt Bedeutung geben will, muss sich auf das einlassen, was er im Sucher rahmt – mit Konzentration, Disziplin, Sensibilität und Sinn für Geometrie [Q4]. Ziel ist der Augenblick, in dem Geschehen und Bildordnung zusammenfallen [Q3].

photographers.name: Robert Frank

portrait.credit: Fotograf unbekannt / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons) – nur 260 px Original, niedrige Auflösung

sources.title: Robert Frank · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Robert Frank American, born Switzerland 1924, Zürich, Switzerland 2019, Nova Scotia, Canada

sources.title: Robert Frank | Howard Greenberg Gallery
sources.excerpt: After graduating from high school, he began an apprenticeship in 1941 with a photographer and retoucher who lived in the same apartment building as Frank's family. The next year, he began to work for the Zurich commercial photographer Michael Wolgensinger who introduced him to Switzerland's active magazine, newspaper, and book publishing industry.

sources.title: Robert Frank | Howard Greenberg Gallery
sources.excerpt: With letters of recommendation from the photographer Walker Evans, as well as Steichen and Brodovitch, he was awarded a fellowship in the spring of 1955 and began to make the photographs that would comprise The Americans . The Americans was published, with an introduction by Jack Kerouac, first in France in 1958 and then in the United States in 1959.

sources.title: Robert Frank | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: The Americans was one of the most revolutionary volumes in the history of photography, and it was a source of controversy when it was published in the United States. Frank's cutting perspective on American culture, combined with his carefree attitude toward traditional photographic technique, shocked most Americans who saw it at the time. During the next decade, however, these qualities of his photography became touchstones for a new generation of American photographers; indeed, Frank's work continues to shape contemporary photography.

sources.title: Robert Frank | Howard Greenberg Gallery
sources.excerpt: In order to create a stronger impact and address larger ideas, he also endeavored to make sequences of his photographs that he hoped would be published in Life or other magazines.

photographers.bio_md: Robert Frank wurde 1924 in Zürich geboren und starb 2019 in Nova Scotia (Kanada) [Q1]. Ab 1941 lernte er bei einem Fotografen und Retuscheur, danach beim Zürcher Werbefotografen Michael Wolgensinger, der ihn mit der Schweizer Magazin- und Verlagswelt bekannt machte [Q2]. Mit Empfehlungen von Walker Evans, Steichen und Brodovitch erhielt er 1955 ein Guggenheim-Stipendium und fotografierte „The Americans“, erschienen 1958 in Frankreich und 1959 in den USA mit einem Vorwort von Jack Kerouac [Q3]. Das Buch gilt als eines der revolutionärsten der Fotografiegeschichte; zunächst umstritten, wurde es für eine neue Generation amerikanischer Fotografen zum Prüfstein [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Frank arbeitete in Sequenzen, um größere Ideen zu tragen und stärker zu wirken [Q5]. Kennzeichnend sind sein schneidender Blick auf die amerikanische Kultur und ein unbekümmerter Umgang mit traditioneller fotografischer Technik [Q4].

photographers.name: Harry Gruyaert

portrait.credit: Profilbild der Magnum-Photos-Fotografenseite (Fotograf des Porträts nicht angegeben); © Magnum Photos, nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Harry Gruyaert • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Harry Gruyaert is known for his extraordinary photographic work with color. Born in Antwerp in 1941, he originally dreamed of becoming a film director. In the late 1970s, Pop art and a trip to Morocco inspired him to become one of the first photographers in Europe to devote his work entirely to color photography.

sources.title: Harry Gruyaert • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Gruyaert's cinematographic background instilled in him an aesthetic conception of photography. Rather than telling stories or documenting the world through his lens, he searches for beauty in everyday elements. His images are simply snapshots of magical moments in which different visual aspects, primarily color, form, light and movement, spontaneously come together in front of his lens.

sources.title: Harry Gruyaert • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: A member of Magnum Photos since 1982, Gruyaert has photographed extensively in the United States, Morocco, Europe, and India. He has also taken many photographs of Belgium, his native country, which have been published in two books: Made in Belgium and Roots .

sources.title: Harry Gruyaert • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: "I was living in London at the end of the 1960s when I became aware of the brainwashing power of television … I became interested in making a portrait of England by photographing the TV screen." - Harry Gruyaert

sources.title: Morocco: An Expression of Enchantment – Harry Gruyaert | Panorama: The Journal of Travel, Place, and Nature
sources.excerpt: Moreover, from my perspective, I don't believe I'm 'communicating' directly with the people I photograph. Concentration and distance are vital to me. If there is 'communication' there, it occurs via a whole mass of visuals, including people but also buildings, fabrics, animals, light and more.

photographers.bio_md: Harry Gruyaert wurde 1941 in Antwerpen geboren und wollte ursprünglich Filmregisseur werden [Q1]. Ende der 1960er fotografierte er in London den Fernsehbildschirm, um ein Porträt Englands zu machen [Q4]. Ende der 1970er brachten ihn Pop-Art und eine Marokko-Reise dazu, als einer der ersten Fotografen Europas ausschließlich in Farbe zu arbeiten [Q1]. Seit 1982 ist er Mitglied von Magnum und fotografierte in den USA, Marokko, Europa und Indien sowie in Belgien („Made in Belgium“, „Roots“) [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Gruyaert erzählt keine Geschichten, sondern sucht das Schöne im Alltäglichen: Momente, in denen Farbe, Form, Licht und Bewegung vor der Kamera spontan zusammenkommen [Q2]. Konzentration und Distanz sind ihm wichtiger als direkte „Kommunikation“ mit den Menschen; das Bild entsteht aus der ganzen Masse des Sichtbaren – Menschen, Gebäude, Stoffe, Tiere, Licht [Q5].

photographers.name: Alec Soth

portrait.credit: Jolson239 / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Alec Soth • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Alec Soth was born in the USA in 1969. He became a nominee of Magnum Photos in 2004 and a full member in 2008. He is based in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

sources.title: Alec Soth • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Likening his process to web surfing in the real world, Soth prizes coincidence and serendipity. Since publishing his first book in 2004, Sleeping by the Mississippi , he has published over 25 books, including his most recent, Advice for Young Artists (2024).

sources.title: Sleeping By The Mississippi • Alec Soth • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Working in a photo-processing lab on other people's pictures throughout his early 20s, he had (almost) given up the ambition to become a famous artist, yet it was this very relaxation of his personal ambition that eventually allowed him the degree of freedom necessary to accept the influence of the American tradition of road trip photography in his own work - to stop pretending he was reinventing the wheel, to carry on the tradition and make it his own.

sources.title: Sleeping By The Mississippi • Alec Soth • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Describing himself as "painfully shy" in his 20s, he knew he had to get over his timidity in order to photograph people; yet he found this very same shyness - coupled with his huge large format box camera and its accompanying tripod - disarmed his subjects, and allowed him a way into their private spaces, following his desire for a deeper intimacy.

sources.title: Sleeping By The Mississippi • Alec Soth • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Having to be very deliberate about each shot of course impacted his process, and delivered the thoughtful, deliberately composed style he is now well-known for.

photographers.bio_md: Alec Soth wurde 1969 in den USA geboren, lebt in Minneapolis und ist seit 2008 Vollmitglied von Magnum [Q1]. In seinen frühen Zwanzigern arbeitete er in einem Fotolabor an den Bildern anderer; erst als er den Ehrgeiz losließ, konnte er die amerikanische Tradition der Roadtrip-Fotografie annehmen und weiterführen [Q3]. Sein erstes Buch „Sleeping by the Mississippi“ erschien 2004; seither hat er über 25 Bücher veröffentlicht [Q2].
photographers.method_md: Soth vergleicht sein Vorgehen mit Websurfen in der realen Welt und setzt auf Zufall und glückliche Fügung [Q2]. Seine große Großformat-Kamera mit Stativ entwaffnete die Porträtierten und öffnete ihm private Räume [Q4]. Weil jede Aufnahme bewusst gesetzt sein musste, entstand sein ruhiger, sorgfältig komponierter Stil [Q5].

photographers.name: Bieke Depoorter

portrait.credit: Profilbild der Magnum-Photos-Fotografenseite (Fotograf des Porträts nicht angegeben); © Magnum Photos, nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Bieke Depoorter • Photographer Profiles • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Born in Belgium in 1986, Bieke Depoorter received a master's degree in photography from the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Ghent in 2009. Three years later, at 25 years old, she was made a nominee of Magnum Photos. She was named a full member in 2016.

sources.title: Bieke Depoorter - Pier 24 Photography
sources.excerpt: In her early work, Depoorter traveled to far-flung locales in Russia, Egypt, and the United States, befriending locals to photograph. She asked her subjects if she could spend the night in their homes, building rapport and trust that eventually allowed her to capture the mundane, routine, ordinary moments of their lives.

sources.title: Bieke Depoorter • Photographer Profiles • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: The relationships Depoorter establishes with the subjects of her photographs lie at the foundation of her artistic practice. Accidental encounters are the starting point. How these interactions naturally develop dictates what follows. Several projects have been the result of Depoorter's constant questioning of the medium itself.

sources.title: Bieke Depoorter • Photographer Profiles • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: In As It May Be , Depoorter gradually became more aware of her status as an outsider, both culturally and as a photographer. So, in 2017, she revisited Egypt with the first draft of the book, inviting people to write comments directly onto the photographs.

sources.title: Bieke Depoorter - Pier 24 Photography
sources.excerpt: Photographer Bieke Depoorter (b. 1986, Belgium) travels the world to find her subjects, creating extraordinarily intimate photographs that straddle portraiture, documentary, and fiction.

photographers.bio_md: Bieke Depoorter wurde 1986 in Belgien geboren und machte 2009 ihren Master in Fotografie an der Königlichen Akademie der Schönen Künste in Gent; 2012 wurde sie Nominee, 2016 Vollmitglied von Magnum [Q1]. In frühen Arbeiten in Russland, Ägypten und den USA bat sie Menschen, bei ihnen übernachten zu dürfen, und fotografierte so den gewöhnlichen Alltag in ihren Wohnungen [Q2]. Für „As It May Be“ kehrte sie 2017 mit dem Buchentwurf nach Ägypten zurück und ließ Menschen direkt auf die Fotos schreiben [Q4]. Ihre sehr intimen Bilder liegen zwischen Porträt, Dokumentation und Fiktion [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Grundlage ihrer Arbeit sind Beziehungen zu den Fotografierten: Zufällige Begegnungen sind der Ausgangspunkt, und wie sich diese entwickeln, bestimmt den weiteren Verlauf [Q3]. Dabei befragt sie immer wieder das Medium selbst [Q3].

photographers.name: Carolyn Drake

portrait.credit: Profilbild der Magnum-Photos-Fotografenseite (Fotograf des Porträts nicht angegeben); © Magnum Photos, nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Carolyn Drake • Photographer Profiles • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Drake was born in California in 1971, and studied media/culture and history at Brown University in the early 1990s. Following her graduation, she moved to New York and worked as an interactive designer for many years before departing to engage with the physical world through photography. After living in Istanbul and Ukraine and working internationally for a decade, she returned to the US in 2013 to work on more self-reflective projects close to home.

sources.title: Carolyn Drake • Photographer Profiles • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Carolyn Drake works on long-term, photo-based projects, seeking to interrogate dominant historical narratives and creatively reimagine them. Her practice embraces collaboration, and has, in recent years, melded photography with sewing, collage, and sculpture. She is interested in collapsing the traditional divides between author and subject, as well as the real and the imaginary.

sources.title: Carolyn Drake – PhotoWork Foundation
sources.excerpt: Between 2007 and 2013, Drake traveled frequently to Central Asia from her base in Istanbul to work on two long term projects. Two Rivers (self-published ,2013) explores the connections between ecology, culture and political power along the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers and earned a 2010 Guggenheim fellowship. Wild Pigeon (self-published, 2014) is an amalgam of photographs, drawings, and embroideries made in collaboration with Uyghurs in western China.

sources.title: Carolyn Drake – PhotoWork Foundation
sources.excerpt: This project was followed by Knit Club (TBW Books, 2020), which emerged from her collaboration with an enigmatic group of women in Mississippi.

sources.title: Carolyn Drake • Photographer Profiles • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Drake has authored four books, with her fifth, Men Untitled , released in September 2023. Her work has been supported by a Guggenheim Fellowship, the Peter S. Reed Foundation, Light Work, the Lange-Taylor Prize, a Fulbright Fellowship and the Henri Cartier-Bresson Award, among others. She became a full member of Magnum Photos in 2019.

photographers.bio_md: Carolyn Drake wurde 1971 in Kalifornien geboren, studierte Anfang der 1990er an der Brown University Medien/Kultur und Geschichte und arbeitete danach lange als Interaktionsdesignerin in New York, bevor sie zur Fotografie wechselte [Q1]. Von Istanbul aus arbeitete sie 2007–2013 in Zentralasien an „Two Rivers“ über Ökologie, Kultur und Macht entlang von Amudarja und Syrdarja sowie an „Wild Pigeon“ mit Uiguren in Westchina [Q3]. 2013 kehrte sie in die USA zurück [Q1]; es folgte u. a. „Knit Club“ (2020) mit einer Gruppe von Frauen in Mississippi [Q4]. Seit 2019 ist sie Vollmitglied von Magnum; 2023 erschien „Men Untitled“ [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Drake arbeitet in langen, fotobasierten Projekten, die herrschende historische Erzählungen befragen und neu denken [Q2]. Ihre Praxis ist kollaborativ und verbindet Fotografie mit Nähen, Collage und Skulptur; sie will die Trennung zwischen Autorin und Subjekt sowie zwischen Realem und Imaginärem aufheben [Q2].

photographers.name: Stephen Shore

portrait.credit: Raphael Labbé aka Leafar / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Stephen Shore | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Born in New York City in 1947, he learned about and practiced photography from the age of six. In 1958, Shore was given a copy of Walker Evans' book American Photographs . This book had a profound effect on him, introducing him to a descriptive visual language of place.

sources.title: Stephen Shore | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: From 1965 through 1967, Shore worked in Andy Warhol's studio, the Factory, a formative experience that allowed him to experiment with combining documentary and conceptual modes in the laconic style characteristic of his later images. In 1971, at the age of twenty-four, Shore had a solo exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the first accorded a living American photographer.

sources.title: Stephen Shore | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Between 1973 and 1979, Shore made a series of road trips across North America, documenting the vernacular landscape through his view camera, and taking a more formal approach to photographing than in his earlier work. A number of these images later formed Shore's now-classic book, Uncommon Places (first published by Aperture in 1982 and republished in 2004 and 2007).

sources.title: Stephen Shore – Sprüth Magers
sources.excerpt: The later series Uncommon Places taken with a large format camera allowed Shore to move away from the snapshot and to make more deliberate, formal and complex images-a different kind of seeing.

sources.title: Stephen Shore – Sprüth Magers
sources.excerpt: Shore's use of color film and large-format camera had a formative influence on a subsequent generation of artists such as Andreas Gursky, Thomas Struth, and Candida Höfer, all of whom became familiar with his work in the photography class of Bernd and Hilla Becher at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf.

photographers.bio_md: Stephen Shore wurde 1947 in New York geboren und fotografierte seit seinem sechsten Lebensjahr; Walker Evans' Buch „American Photographs“ führte ihn 1958 an eine beschreibende Bildsprache des Ortes heran [Q1]. 1965–1967 arbeitete er in Andy Warhols Factory, wo er dokumentarische und konzeptuelle Ansätze im lakonischen Stil seiner späteren Bilder verband; 1971 zeigte das Metropolitan Museum ihn als ersten lebenden amerikanischen Fotografen in einer Einzelausstellung [Q2]. Auf Roadtrips 1973–1979 fotografierte er die alltägliche Landschaft Nordamerikas; daraus entstand das Buch „Uncommon Places“ (1982) [Q3]. Seine Farb- und Großformatarbeit prägte über die Becher-Klasse in Düsseldorf Gursky, Struth und Höfer [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Für „Uncommon Places“ arbeitete Shore mit der Fachkamera und formaler als zuvor [Q3]. Das Großformat führte ihn weg vom Schnappschuss hin zu bewussteren, formalen und komplexeren Bildern – „eine andere Art zu sehen“ [Q4].

photographers.name: Robert Adams

portrait.credit: Sonia Lenzi / CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Robert Adams (Getty Center Exhibitions)
sources.excerpt: For more than 40 years, Robert Adams (born 1937) has photographed the landscape of the American West, particularly in California, Oregon, and his home state of Colorado. His work is inspired both by his joy in the inherent beauty of the landscape, and his dismay at its exploitation and degradation for residential and commercial development.

sources.title: Robert Adams | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Originally from Orange, New Jersey, Robert Adams came to photography in 1963 when earning a Ph.D in English at the University of Southern California. While teaching English at Colorado College in 1967, he photographed residential areas around Colorado Springs at the request of the organizers of a conference on the western landscape.

sources.title: Robert Adams | Fraenkel Gallery
sources.excerpt: In the 1970s and '80s Adams produced a series of books- The New West , Denver , What We Bought , Summer Nights -that focused on expanding suburbs along Colorado's Front Range, books that pictured heedless development but also the surviving light, scale, form, and silence of the natural world.

sources.title: Robert Adams | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: He was included in the 1975 exhibition New Topographics: Photographs of a Man-Altered Landscape at the George Eastman House, which associated his work with that of Lewis Baltz and Stephen Shore, among others.

sources.title: Robert Adams (Getty Center Exhibitions)
sources.excerpt: About his 1970s work, published under the title The New West , Adams wrote, "The subject of these pictures is...the source of all Form, light." He asserted, "I love the light," underscoring that the deeper subject of these pictures is not the tract homes or freeways they depict.

photographers.bio_md: Robert Adams (geb. 1937) fotografiert seit über 40 Jahren die Landschaft des amerikanischen Westens, besonders in Kalifornien, Oregon und Colorado – aus Freude an ihrer Schönheit und aus Bestürzung über ihre Zerstörung durch Bebauung [Q1]. Er stammt aus Orange (New Jersey) und kam 1963 während seiner Promotion in Englisch zur Fotografie; als Englischdozent am Colorado College fotografierte er 1967 Wohngebiete um Colorado Springs [Q2]. In den 1970ern und 1980ern entstanden Bücher wie „The New West“, „Denver“, „What We Bought“ und „Summer Nights“ über die wachsenden Vororte an der Front Range [Q3]. 1975 war er Teil der Ausstellung „New Topographics“ im George Eastman House, neben Lewis Baltz und Stephen Shore [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Adams zeigt rücksichtslose Bebauung und zugleich das, was von Licht, Maßstab, Form und Stille der Natur übrig bleibt [Q3]. Das eigentliche Thema seiner Bilder ist nach eigener Aussage nicht das Reihenhaus oder die Autobahn, sondern das Licht [Q5].

photographers.name: Steve McCurry

portrait.credit: Christopher Michel / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Steve McCurry • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Born in 1950, Steve McCurry is an American photographer who has been working for more than four decades. He has published over 20 books and has had scores of major exhibitions at museums around the world. He joined Magnum Photos in 1986 and is now a contributor.

sources.title: Steve McCurry • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: It was after several months of travel that he met a group of refugees from Afghanistan, who smuggled him across the border into their country, just as the Russian invasion was unfolding. Emerging after weeks embedded with the Mujahideen, McCurry brought the world the first images of the Soviet assault in Afghanistan.

sources.title: Steve McCurry: McCurry's India | Amateur Photographer
sources.excerpt: Most photographers have at some time recognised a composition, perhaps a poster or something on the wall, and waited for a person or animal or car to complete the picture. There are times when you recognise a design or a composition, and you work it; if you think it's worth it, you'll wait for as long as it takes.

sources.title: Steve McCurry: McCurry's India | Amateur Photographer
sources.excerpt: I used Kodachrome for over 20 years. It was my mainstay, probably the best film ever made.

sources.title: Steve McCurry • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: "What is important to my work is the individual picture. I photograph stories on assignment, and of course they have to be put together coherently. But what matters most is that each picture stands on its own, with its own place and feeling." - Steve McCurry

photographers.bio_md: Steve McCurry, geboren 1950, ist ein amerikanischer Fotograf, der seit über vier Jahrzehnten arbeitet, mehr als 20 Bücher veröffentlicht hat und 1986 zu Magnum kam [Q1]. Nach dem Studium reiste er durch Indien; afghanische Flüchtlinge schmuggelten ihn über die Grenze, und nach Wochen bei den Mudschahedin brachte er die ersten Bilder des sowjetischen Einmarschs in Afghanistan [Q2]. Über 20 Jahre war Kodachrome sein wichtigstes Material [Q4].
photographers.method_md: McCurry erkennt eine Komposition – etwa ein Plakat oder eine Wand – und wartet, bis ein Mensch, Tier oder Auto das Bild vervollständigt, notfalls sehr lange [Q3]. Auch bei Reportagen zählt für ihn vor allem das Einzelbild, das für sich stehen muss, mit eigenem Ort und Gefühl [Q5].

photographers.name: William Eggleston

sources.title: William Eggleston - Artworks & Biography | David Zwirner
sources.excerpt: Eggleston was born in Memphis, Tennessee, where he continues to live today. Raised in Sumner, Mississippi, he attended Vanderbilt University, Nashville; Delta State College, Cleveland, Mississippi; and University of Mississippi, Oxford.

sources.title: William Eggleston - Artworks & Biography | David Zwirner
sources.excerpt: Over the course of nearly six decades, William Eggleston (b. 1939) has established a singular pictorial style that deftly combines vernacular subject matter with an innate and sophisticated understanding of color, form, and composition. His photographs transform the ordinary into distinctive, poetic images that eschew fixed meaning.

sources.title: William Eggleston - Artworks & Biography | David Zwirner
sources.excerpt: His 1976 solo exhibition at The Museum of Modern Art, New York, curated by John Szarkowski, marked one of the first presentations of color photography at the museum. Although initially criticized for its unfamiliar approach, the show and its accompanying catalogue, William Eggleston's Guide , heralded an important moment in the medium's acceptance within the art-historical canon, and it solidified the artist's position as one of its foremost practitioners to this date.

sources.title: William Eggleston - Artworks & Biography | David Zwirner
sources.excerpt: American artist William Eggleston's discovery of the dye-transfer process in the 1970s-primarily used in advertising at the time-was crucial to his move from primarily working in black-and-white to producing color photographs due to the richness of tonal depth and color saturation.

sources.title: William Eggleston: Afterward from 'The Democratic Forest' (1988) – American Suburb X
sources.excerpt: I was treating things democratically, which of course didn't mean a thing to the people I was talking to.

photographers.bio_md: William Eggleston (geb. 1939) wurde in Memphis (Tennessee) geboren, wo er bis heute lebt; er wuchs in Sumner (Mississippi) auf und besuchte die Vanderbilt University, das Delta State College und die University of Mississippi [Q1]. Seine Einzelausstellung 1976 im Museum of Modern Art, kuratiert von John Szarkowski, war eine der ersten Präsentationen von Farbfotografie dort; zunächst kritisiert, markierten Schau und Katalog „William Eggleston's Guide“ einen wichtigen Schritt zur Anerkennung des Mediums [Q3]. Über fast sechs Jahrzehnte entwickelte er einen unverwechselbaren Stil aus alltäglichen Motiven und souveränem Gespür für Farbe, Form und Komposition [Q2].
photographers.method_md: Die Entdeckung des Farbstoffübertragungsverfahrens (Dye-Transfer) in den 1970ern – damals vor allem in der Werbung genutzt – war wegen seiner Tonwerttiefe und Farbsättigung entscheidend für Egglestons Wechsel zur Farbe [Q4]. Er behandelte die Dinge „demokratisch“, ohne Hierarchie der Motive [Q5].

photographers.name: Joel Meyerowitz

portrait.credit: Hans Peter Schaefer Hps-poll / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Joel Meyerowitz | Howard Greenberg Gallery
sources.excerpt: Joel Meyerowitz (b. 1938) was born in New York City and began taking photographs in 1962. Although he has always seen himself as a street photographer in the tradition of Henri Cartier-Bresson and Robert Frank (he is the co-author of the standard work on the genre, Bystander: A History of Street Photography , 1994) he transformed the mode with his pioneering use of color.

sources.title: Joel Meyerowitz | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Joel Meyerowitz studied painting and medical drawing at Ohio State University, where he received a BFA in 1959, and initially worked as an advertising art director in his native New York City. He taught himself photography after collaborating on an advertising project with Robert Frank in 1962. Inspired by Frank, his early work consisted mainly of black-and-white street photographs made with a Leica; by 1976 he had turned primarily to color photographs of architectural light and space made with a large-format view camera.

sources.title: Cape Light - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: Joel Meyerowitz went to Cape Cod, Massachusetts, with a vintage 8 x 10 inch Deardoff view camera seeking a different kind of photography to the type he had become accustomed to making with his Leica in New York. The resulting book of photographs, Cape Light , first published in 1978, is now regarded as one of the most significant photobooks of the twentieth century.

sources.title: Cape Light - Huxley-Parlour Gallery
sources.excerpt: The large format camera required him to step back from his usual proximity to his subjects on the streets of New York and take in his larger surroundings.

sources.title: Joel Meyerowitz | Howard Greenberg Gallery
sources.excerpt: Meyerowitz was the only photographer to be given unimpeded access to Ground Zero in the wake of 9/11. The images he captured have formed the foundation of a major national archive, and an exhibition of selected images has travelled to more than 200 cities in 60 countries.

photographers.bio_md: Joel Meyerowitz (geb. 1938) stammt aus New York und fotografiert seit 1962; er versteht sich als Straßenfotograf in der Tradition von Cartier-Bresson und Robert Frank, veränderte das Genre aber durch frühe Farbfotografie [Q1]. Er studierte Malerei und medizinisches Zeichnen an der Ohio State University, arbeitete als Art Director und brachte sich die Fotografie nach einem Werbeprojekt mit Robert Frank 1962 selbst bei [Q2]. „Cape Light“ (1978) gilt heute als eines der bedeutendsten Fotobücher des 20. Jahrhunderts [Q3]. Nach dem 11. September erhielt er als einziger Fotograf freien Zugang zu Ground Zero [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Anfangs fotografierte Meyerowitz schwarzweiß mit der Leica auf der Straße, ab 1976 vor allem in Farbe mit der Großformat-Fachkamera – Licht und Raum der Architektur [Q2]. Die 8×10-Zoll-Kamera in Cape Cod zwang ihn, von der Nähe der Straßenfotografie zurückzutreten und die weitere Umgebung aufzunehmen [Q3][Q4].

photographers.name: Lewis Baltz

portrait.credit: Slavica Perkovic / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Lewis Baltz - Zander Galerie
sources.excerpt: Lewis Baltz (1945-2014) critically expanded the documentary discourse and was instrumental in conceptual photography taking its place in contemporary art since the 1960s. Born in Newport Beach, California, Baltz witnessed rapid suburban expansion with its increasingly dominant industrial and corporate architecture, which became central to his work.

sources.title: Lewis Baltz - Zander Galerie
sources.excerpt: Alongside Bernd and Hilla Becher, Stephen Shore, and Henry Wessel, Baltz was among the renowned artists of the landmark exhibition "New Topographics: Photographs of a Man-Altered Landscape" (1975) at The George Eastman House in Rochester, New York, which marked a major shift in landscape photography.

sources.title: Fast World, Slow Photography: Lewis Baltz | David Campany
sources.excerpt: They come from a series of 51 images titled "The New Industrial Parks Near Irvine, California". In Irvine, a newly built suburban city south of Los Angeles, Baltz was studying the emergence of what is now very familiar: those generic structures of little architectural merit that cluster on the edge of towns and cities.

sources.title: Fast World, Slow Photography: Lewis Baltz | David Campany
sources.excerpt: "I didn't want to have a style; I wanted my photography to look as mute and as distant as to appear to be as objective as possible. I tried very hard not to show a point of view. I tried to think of myself as an anthropologist from a different solar system."

sources.title: Fast World, Slow Photography: Lewis Baltz | David Campany
sources.excerpt: Baltz couldn't be bothered with all that heavy gear so he used, of all things, a lightweight Leica - a camera designed for taking snapshots on the fly. It had a superb lens and Baltz reckoned that with a tripod, fine-grained film and great discipline in the darkroom he could get what he was after.

photographers.bio_md: Lewis Baltz (1945–2014) erweiterte den dokumentarischen Diskurs und trug dazu bei, dass konzeptuelle Fotografie ihren Platz in der Gegenwartskunst fand [Q1]. Geboren in Newport Beach (Kalifornien), erlebte er die rasche Ausbreitung der Vororte mit ihrer Industrie- und Firmenarchitektur, die zum Zentrum seines Werks wurde [Q1]. 1975 gehörte er mit den Bechers, Stephen Shore und Henry Wessel zur Ausstellung „New Topographics“, die eine Wende in der Landschaftsfotografie markierte [Q2]. Seine Serie „The New Industrial Parks Near Irvine, California“ (51 Bilder) untersucht die anonymen Zweckbauten am Rand der Städte [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Baltz wollte keinen Stil, sondern Bilder, die so stumm und distanziert wie möglich wirken – „wie ein Anthropologe aus einem anderen Sonnensystem“ [Q4]. Statt Großformat nutzte er eine leichte Leica mit Stativ, feinkörnigem Film und großer Disziplin in der Dunkelkammer [Q5].

photographers.name: Frank Gohlke

sources.title: Accommodating Nature: The Photographs of Frank Gohlke | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: For more than 30 years, Frank Gohlke (b. 1942 ), a leading figure in American landscape photography, has explored the ways Americans build their lives in a natural world that rarely fits within a traditional pastoral ideal.

sources.title: Retrospective of Photographer Frank Gohlke Organized by the Amon Carter Museum
sources.excerpt: Gohlke received his BA from the University of Texas at Austin in English literature. At Yale University, where he received his MA in English in 1966, Gohlke met Walker Evans and then studied privately with Paul Caponigro.

sources.title: Retrospective of Photographer Frank Gohlke Organized by the Amon Carter Museum
sources.excerpt: "Frank Gohlke helped lead a fundamental shift in how we think about landscape art," Rohrbach explains. "Early in his career, he was one of an influential group of photographers who redefined American landscape not as grand vistas of untouched nature but as scenes shaped by the built environment.

sources.title: Accommodating Nature: The Photographs of Frank Gohlke | Smithsonian American Art Museum
sources.excerpt: Whether photographing his hometown of Wichita Falls, Texas; the grain elevators that punctuate the vast spaces of the Midwest; the effect of the 1980 volcanic eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington; or the neighborhoods of Queens, NY, Gohlke deftly captures the tension between humanity and the natural world, exploring how people adapt to the forces of nature both great and small, even within the confines of their own backyards.

sources.title: Retrospective of Photographer Frank Gohlke Organized by the Amon Carter Museum
sources.excerpt: By focusing on renewal and regrowth rather than on disaster, they raise provocative questions about human agency and our compulsion to continuously reassert ourselves.

photographers.bio_md: Frank Gohlke (geb. 1942) ist eine führende Figur der amerikanischen Landschaftsfotografie und untersucht seit über 30 Jahren, wie Menschen ihr Leben in einer Natur einrichten, die selten einem pastoralen Ideal entspricht [Q1]. Er studierte Englische Literatur in Austin und Yale (MA 1966), lernte dort Walker Evans kennen und studierte danach privat bei Paul Caponigro [Q2]. Er gehörte zu einer einflussreichen Gruppe, die die amerikanische Landschaft nicht als unberührte Weite, sondern als vom Gebauten geprägte Szene neu bestimmte [Q3]. Zu seinen Themen zählen seine Heimatstadt Wichita Falls, die Getreidesilos des Mittleren Westens, der Ausbruch des Mount St. Helens 1980 und Viertel in Queens [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Gohlke zeigt die Spannung zwischen Mensch und Natur und wie Menschen sich großen und kleinen Naturkräften anpassen, bis in den eigenen Garten [Q4]. Nach Katastrophen wie dem Vulkanausbruch richtet er den Blick auf Erneuerung und Nachwachsen statt auf die Zerstörung [Q5].

photographers.name: Bernd und Hilla Becher

portrait.credit: Praemium Erasmianum Foundation / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons) – Erasmuspreis-Verleihung 2002, die Bechers mit einer dritten Person

sources.title: Bernd & Hilla Becher | Mirabaud Contemporary Art Collection
sources.excerpt: Bernhard Becher was born in Siegen near Cologne in 1931. He first studied painting at the Staatliche Kunstakademie in Stuttgart and later typography at the Düsseldorf Kunstakademie from 1959 to 1961. Hilla Wobeser was born in 1934 in Postdam, near Berlin. As her mother and uncle were both photographers, she trained early in photography with the plate-camera she had received.

sources.title: Bernd & Hilla Becher | Mirabaud Contemporary Art Collection
sources.excerpt: They began photographing together in 1959. Their first exhibition in Düsseldorf in 1969 was entitled Anonymous Sculptures , and the subsequent eponymous book brought them fame in the United States where they exhibited at the George Eastman House and the Sonnabend Gallery as early as 1972.

sources.title: Bernd & Hilla Becher | Mirabaud Contemporary Art Collection
sources.excerpt: Through their objective approach, always photographing in black and white with a large 8x10 inch view camera under overcast, neutral skies and from the same frontal and elevated perspective, the isolated structures became sculptures. To heighten the effect, the photographs were presented in grids of 3 by 3, 4 or 5, creating large-scale installations highlighting the structures' formal similarities.

sources.title: Bernd & Hilla Becher | Mirabaud Contemporary Art Collection
sources.excerpt: Their stylistic lineage can be traced to the German movement, the Neue Sachlichkeit (New Objectivity), and the work of Karl Blossfeld and August Sander. In turn, after two decades teaching at the Düsseldorf Kunstakademie, they influenced an entire new generation of now-famous photographers including Andreas Gursky, Thomas Ruff, Thomas Struth and Candida Höfer.

sources.title: Bernd & Hilla Becher | Mirabaud Contemporary Art Collection
sources.excerpt: They won the Golden Lion of the Venice Biennale in 1990 for sculpture, the Erasmus Prize in 2002 and the Hasselblad Photography Award in 2004. They lived in Düsseldorf. Bernd Becher died in 2007 and Hilla Becher in 2015.

photographers.bio_md: Bernd Becher wurde 1931 in Siegen geboren und studierte Malerei in Stuttgart, dann Typografie an der Düsseldorfer Kunstakademie; Hilla Wobeser, 1934 in Potsdam geboren, lernte früh mit der Plattenkamera zu fotografieren, da Mutter und Onkel Fotografen waren [Q1]. Ab 1959 fotografierten sie gemeinsam; ihre erste Ausstellung 1969 hieß „Anonyme Skulpturen“, das gleichnamige Buch machte sie auch in den USA bekannt [Q2]. Ihre Linie reicht zur Neuen Sachlichkeit, zu Karl Blossfeldt und August Sander; als Lehrer an der Düsseldorfer Akademie prägten sie Andreas Gursky, Thomas Ruff, Thomas Struth und Candida Höfer [Q4]. Sie erhielten 1990 den Goldenen Löwen der Biennale Venedig für Skulptur und 2004 den Hasselblad-Preis; Bernd Becher starb 2007, Hilla Becher 2015 [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Die Bechers fotografierten stets schwarzweiß mit der 8×10-Zoll-Fachkamera bei bedecktem, neutralem Himmel, frontal und aus erhöhtem Standpunkt; so wurden die isolierten Bauten zu Skulpturen [Q3]. Präsentiert wurden sie in Rastern (Typologien), die formale Ähnlichkeiten sichtbar machen [Q3].

photographers.name: Ernst Haas

portrait.credit: Rochester Institute of Technology / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Ernst Haas | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Ernst Haas was born in Vienna and began studying photography at the Graphische Lehr und Versuchsanstalt in Vienna six years before acquiring his first camera in 1946.

sources.title: Ernst Haas | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: After several photography-related jobs, he was offered a position at Life , and his first feature article, "Returning Prisoners of War," was published in both Heute and Life in 1949. This prompted Robert Capa to invite Haas to join the Magnum agency, the international cooperative founded by Capa, Henri Cartier-Bresson, George Rodger and Chim (David Seymour).

sources.title: Ernst Haas | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Also in 1949, Haas purchased a Leica and began experimenting with color photography, the medium in which his work is best known. His "Magic Images of New York," a twenty-four-page color photo essay, which appeared in LIFE in 1951 was both his and LIFE 's first long color feature in print.

sources.title: Ernst Haas | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Ernst Haas pioneered the use of color photography at a time when it was considered inferior to black-and-white as a medium for serious creative photographers. His innovative use of the slow shutter speed, which gave many of his pictures the illusion of movement, and his emphasis on audiovisual presentations (works involving sound, poetry, and pictures) opened many possibilities in color photography and in multimedia art.

sources.title: Ernst Haas | International Center of Photography
sources.excerpt: Artist 1921 - 1986 American

photographers.bio_md: Ernst Haas (1921–1986) [Q5] wurde in Wien geboren und studierte dort an der Graphischen Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt, bevor er 1946 seine erste Kamera bekam [Q1]. Nach seiner Reportage über heimkehrende Kriegsgefangene (1949 in „Heute“ und „Life“) lud Robert Capa ihn zu Magnum ein [Q2]. 1951 erschien in „Life“ sein 24-seitiger Farbessay „Magic Images of New York“, die erste lange Farbstrecke des Magazins [Q3]. Haas setzte die Farbfotografie durch, als sie für ernsthafte Fotografen noch als minderwertig galt [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Seit 1949 arbeitete Haas mit der Leica in Farbe [Q3]. Lange Belichtungszeiten erzeugten in vielen Bildern den Eindruck von Bewegung; dazu kamen audiovisuelle Präsentationen mit Ton, Poesie und Bildern [Q4].

photographers.name: Michael Wolf

portrait.credit: „A portrait of Michael Wolf, the photographer“, Cathay Pacific Discovery-Magazin (Fotograf nicht angegeben); nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Biography | Michael Wolf Photography
sources.excerpt: the focus of the german photographer michael wolf's work is life in mega cities. many of his projects document the architecture and the vernacular culture of metropolises. wolf grew up in canada, europe and the united states, studying at uc berkeley and at the folkwang school with otto steinert in essen, germany. he moved to hong kong in 1994 where he worked for 8 years as contract photographer for stern magazine.

sources.title: Paying tribute to photographer Michael Wolf | Cathay Pacific
sources.excerpt: The 64-year-old German was one of the preeminent documenters of Hong Kong's congested urban life, and had resided here for the majority of the past 25 years. He died in his home on the island of Cheung Chau on 24 April 2019. He was perhaps most notable for his series Architecture of Density , which framed Hong Kong's supertall high-rises and housing estates and the people within.

sources.title: Paying tribute to photographer Michael Wolf | Cathay Pacific
sources.excerpt: You'll see everything from his 1976 university thesis, for which he spent a year documenting a coal-mining community in the Ruhr, Germany; through to his best-known artistic works such as Tokyo Compression and Architecture of Density; to his latest project, Informal Solutions, which documents the ways Hongkongers recycle, reuse and adapt everyday products.

sources.title: Paying tribute to photographer Michael Wolf | Cathay Pacific
sources.excerpt: Wolf's project A Series of Unfortunate Events, in which he photographed scenes from Google Street View on his monitor, inspired some to accuse him of laziness. 'It's a misconception,' he says. 'I spent six months, five or six hours a day sitting in a dark room in Paris, going through the streets of Paris on my monitor, and it's hard work. I decide what to photograph, I crop and make my composition, so it's hairbrained to say it's not photography.'

sources.title: Biography | Michael Wolf Photography
sources.excerpt: he has won first prize in the world press photo award competition on two occasions (2005 & 2010) and an honorable mention (2011.) in 2010, wolf was shortlisted for the prix pictet photography prize.

photographers.bio_md: Michael Wolf war ein deutscher Fotograf, der in Kanada, Europa und den USA aufwuchs und an der UC Berkeley sowie bei Otto Steinert an der Folkwangschule in Essen studierte; 1994 zog er nach Hongkong und arbeitete acht Jahre als Vertragsfotograf für den „Stern“ [Q1]. Sein Thema ist das Leben in Megastädten, ihre Architektur und Alltagskultur [Q1]. Bekannt wurde er vor allem mit „Architecture of Density“ über Hongkongs Hochhäuser und Wohnsiedlungen; er starb am 24. April 2019 auf Cheung Chau [Q2]. Sein Werk reicht von der Diplomarbeit 1976 über eine Bergarbeitersiedlung im Ruhrgebiet bis zu „Tokyo Compression“ und „Informal Solutions“ [Q3].
