Er gewann zweimal einen ersten Preis bei World Press Photo (2005, 2010) [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Für „A Series of Unfortunate Events“ fotografierte Wolf Szenen aus Google Street View vom Bildschirm ab; er bestand darauf, dass Auswahl, Beschnitt und Komposition ihn auch dort zum Fotografen machen [Q4].

photographers.name: Andreas Gursky

portrait.credit: Hpschaefer www.reserv-art.de / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Andreas Gursky | biography
sources.excerpt: Born in Leipzig, Germany, 1955 Lives and works in Düsseldorf, Germany Jahr Text 2010 – 2018 professorship for Liberal Arts at the Art Academy in Düsseldorf, Germany 1980 – 1987 Art Academy Düsseldorf, Germany Studies with Bernd Becher and Kasper König (master student of Bernd Becher 1985) 1977 – 1980 Folkwang University of the Arts, Essen, Germany Studies with Michael Schmidt

sources.title: Andreas Gursky – Sprüth Magers
sources.excerpt: Andreas Gursky (*1955) is considered one of the most important photographers in the world, an artist who has expanded the boundaries of the photographic medium like few before him. His complex, large-format images-some of which have attained iconic status-show spectacular landscapes and elaborate interiors, combining technical virtuosity with a painterly eye. His work casts a relentless gaze on the age of globalization, rigorously dissecting the effects of modernity.

sources.title: Andreas Gursky – Sprüth Magers
sources.excerpt: The supersized photographs typical of Gursky, some of which have the dimensions of smaller cinema screens, merge a hyperreal view of the whole with an extraordinary abundance of detail. Their foreground and background have the same depth of field. It is physically impossible for the viewer to take in the entire image and its excess of meticulously-captured details all at once.

sources.title: Andreas Gursky – Sprüth Magers
sources.excerpt: Gursky employs digital techniques in a variety of ways: to remove or add pictorial elements, emphasize details, seamlessly assemble an image from smaller photographs or manipulate perspective. In general, these interventions seem to aim at overwhelming the viewer with detail, creating a particularly Gursky-esque version of the sublime.

sources.title: Andreas Gursky: Interview with Insight – Canadian Art
sources.excerpt: He shoots on film with a five-by-seven camera and scans images into the computer in order to retouch, manipulate and build them as montage.

photographers.bio_md: Andreas Gursky wurde 1955 in Leipzig geboren und lebt in Düsseldorf; er studierte 1977–1980 an der Folkwang-Hochschule in Essen bei Michael Schmidt und 1980–1987 an der Düsseldorfer Kunstakademie bei Bernd Becher (Meisterschüler 1985) [Q1]. Er gilt als einer der wichtigsten Fotografen der Welt; seine großformatigen Bilder zeigen spektakuläre Landschaften und aufwendige Innenräume und richten einen unerbittlichen Blick auf das Zeitalter der Globalisierung [Q2]. 2010–2018 war er selbst Professor an der Düsseldorfer Akademie [Q1].
photographers.method_md: Gursky fotografiert auf Film mit einer 5×7-Zoll-Kamera, scannt die Aufnahmen und retuschiert, verändert und montiert sie am Computer [Q5]. Digital entfernt oder ergänzt er Bildelemente, setzt Bilder aus Teilaufnahmen zusammen oder verändert die Perspektive [Q4]. Die riesigen Abzüge verbinden einen hyperrealen Gesamtblick mit gleichmäßiger Schärfe von vorn bis hinten und einer Fülle an Details, die man nie auf einmal erfassen kann [Q3].

photographers.name: Thomas Struth

portrait.credit: Hpschaefer www.reserv-art.de / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Thomas Struth - Städel Museum Digital Collection
sources.excerpt: Thomas Struth was born in 1954 in Geldern, near the border between Germany and Holland. Between 1973 and 1980 he attended the art academy in Düsseldorf, studying first painting under Gerhard Richter and finally photography under Bernd and Hilla Becher.

sources.title: Thomas Struth - Städel Museum Digital Collection
sources.excerpt: His early photographs of New York are sober cityscapes, but in the mid-1980s he turned more and more towards portraits, both pictures of families and single subjects. In his well-known series of museum photographs he captured visitors viewing works of art.

sources.title: Thomas Struth | ZKM
sources.excerpt: A coolly distanced, unsentimental view of the subject and the tendency to work in series characterize the endeavour to achieve an objective representation, behind which the photographer retreats.

sources.title: Thomas Struth | ZKM
sources.excerpt: The images are distinguished by their calculated cropping and the rigour of their composition. The construction of each picture is dominated by clear central perspective, emphasized above all in the street scenes.

sources.title: Interview with Thomas Struth: "Photographs reveal people's inner agenda" - The Art Newspaper
sources.excerpt: I wanted this to be the title of my first big exhibition at the Kunsthalle Berne [in 1987] because I wanted to highlight that this work was not so much about architectural styles or urban history but about what communities created beyond individual responsibilities of architects and financiers, building laws and stuff like that.

photographers.bio_md: Thomas Struth wurde 1954 in Geldern am Niederrhein geboren und studierte 1973–1980 an der Düsseldorfer Kunstakademie, zuerst Malerei bei Gerhard Richter, dann Fotografie bei Bernd und Hilla Becher [Q1]. Nach nüchternen Stadtansichten wandte er sich ab Mitte der 1980er Porträts zu – Familien wie Einzelpersonen; bekannt wurde er mit den Museumsbildern, die Besucher vor Kunstwerken zeigen [Q2]. Seine menschenleeren Straßenbilder nannte er „Unbewusste Orte“: Es ging ihm nicht um Baustile, sondern darum, was Gemeinschaften jenseits einzelner Verantwortlicher schaffen [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Struth arbeitet mit kühl distanziertem, unsentimentalem Blick und in Serien; der Fotograf tritt hinter eine möglichst objektive Darstellung zurück [Q3]. Seine Bilder zeichnen sich durch kalkulierten Ausschnitt, strenge Komposition und eine klare Zentralperspektive aus, besonders in den Straßenbildern [Q4].

photographers.name: Candida Höfer

portrait.credit: Hpschaefer / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Candida Höfer - Artists - Sean Kelly Gallery
sources.excerpt: Born in Eberswalde, Germany in 1944, Candida Höfer attended the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf from 1973 to 1982. Whilst there she studied film with the Danish filmmaker Ole John and photography under the influential photographers Bernd and Hilla Becher, who also taught noted Düsseldorf School photographers Andreas Gursky, Thomas Struth, Axel Hütte and Thomas Ruff.

sources.title: Candida Höfer - Artists - Sean Kelly Gallery
sources.excerpt: Known for her meticulously composed, large-scale color images of architectural interiors, Höfer's oeuvre explores the structure, presentation, and influence of space. Interested in the psychological impact of design and the contrast between a room's intended and actual use, Höfer has focused her lens on cultural and institutional buildings such as libraries, hotels, museums, concert halls, and palaces.

sources.title: Candida Höfer - Artists - Sean Kelly Gallery
sources.excerpt: On her decision to exclude people from her photographs, Höfer has said, "…it became apparent to me that what people do in these spaces - and what these spaces do to them - is clearer when no one is present, just as an absent guest is often the subject of a conversation."

sources.title: Candida Höfer - Artists - Sean Kelly Gallery
sources.excerpt: Höfer represented Germany at the 2003 Venice Biennale. In 2018, the Sony World Photography Awards recognized Candida Höfer for her outstanding contribution to photography.

sources.title: Dusseldorf School of Photography | Tate
sources.excerpt: The Dusseldorf School of Photography refers to a group of photographers who studied at the Kunstakademie Dusseldorf in the mid 1970s under the influential photographers Bernd and Hilla Becher

photographers.bio_md: Candida Höfer wurde 1944 in Eberswalde geboren und studierte 1973–1982 an der Kunstakademie Düsseldorf Film bei Ole John und Fotografie bei Bernd und Hilla Becher [Q1]. Sie zählt damit zur Düsseldorfer Schule, den Schülern der Bechers an der Akademie [Q5]. Bekannt ist sie für sorgfältig komponierte, großformatige Farbaufnahmen von Innenräumen öffentlicher Bauten wie Bibliotheken, Hotels, Museen, Konzertsäle und Paläste [Q2]. 2003 vertrat sie Deutschland auf der Biennale Venedig [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Höfer interessiert die psychologische Wirkung von Gestaltung und der Gegensatz zwischen geplanter und tatsächlicher Nutzung eines Raums [Q2]. Sie lässt Menschen weg, weil gerade dann deutlicher wird, was Menschen in diesen Räumen tun und was die Räume mit ihnen machen [Q3].

photographers.name: Herbert Ponting

portrait.credit: Ponting, Herbert George, copyright claimant / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: New Exhibition – Herbert Ponting: Explorer and Photographer - The Atkinson
sources.excerpt: After years of taking photographs in America, Japan, other parts of Asia and in Europe, Herbert Ponting (1870-1935) became and remains best-known for his work on Captain Scott's Terra Nova expedition (1910-3).

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Ponting, Herbert George
sources.excerpt: He moved to California where he married Mary Biddle Elliott in 1895 and ran a fruit ranch. In 1900 after the fruit ranch proved commercially unviable Ponting turned to photography to support his young family, ironically it was his photographic career which ultimately resulted in him deserting his family.

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Ponting, Herbert George
sources.excerpt: He travelled widely in the Far East, South-East Asia and Europe and was a pioneer in the use of the camera as a medium of art rather than a mere recorder of events and persons. From 1904-05 he covered the Russo-Japanese War for Harpers Weekly. In 1910 he published his first illustrated book In Lotus Land Japan this resulted in Ponting being recognised internationally as a popular photographer and travel writer.

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Ponting, Herbert George
sources.excerpt: The technical difficulties of photography in the Antarctic were formidable but Ponting overcame these problems by his technical mastery. He built himself a small darkroom in one of the huts at Cape Evans. Here he spent 14 months, producing over 1000 photographs.

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Ponting, Herbert George
sources.excerpt: Ponting strived to get the perfect photograph and often put himself or expedition members in risky situations, for example constructing hoists to hold himself and his equipment over the edge of the ship in order to get the exact shot he desired.

photographers.bio_md: Herbert Ponting (1870–1935) fotografierte jahrelang in Amerika, Japan, Asien und Europa, bekannt ist er aber vor allem für seine Arbeit auf Scotts Terra-Nova-Expedition 1910–1913 [Q1]. In Kalifornien betrieb er eine Obstfarm; als diese 1900 scheiterte, wandte er sich der Fotografie zu, um seine Familie zu ernähren [Q2]. Er reiste durch Ostasien, Südostasien und Europa, berichtete 1904–05 für Harper's Weekly vom Russisch-Japanischen Krieg und wurde mit dem Japan-Buch „In Lotus Land Japan“ (1910) international bekannt [Q3]. Er gilt als Pionier, der die Kamera als künstlerisches Medium statt als bloßes Aufzeichnungsgerät verstand [Q3].
photographers.method_md: In der Antarktis meisterte Ponting die technischen Schwierigkeiten mit großer Könnerschaft; in einer kleinen Dunkelkammer in Cape Evans entstanden in 14 Monaten über 1000 Fotos [Q4]. Für das perfekte Bild ging er Risiken ein, etwa mit Seilzügen, die ihn samt Ausrüstung über die Bordwand hielten [Q5].

photographers.name: Frank Hurley

portrait.credit: Frank Hurley / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Hurley, James Francis (Frank)
sources.excerpt: Hurley, James Francis (Frank) (1885-1962) Born in Sydney, Australia in 1885. He left school without qualifications and worked in a steel mill before completing his education at the University of Sydney.

sources.title: Frank Hurley OBE - The Australian Museum
sources.excerpt: When he returned he bought a Kodak box camera and taught himself photography. At the age of 20, he joined a postcard business in Sydney and earned a reputation for both high-quality photographs and the risks he took to secure them (such as facing monstrous waves breaking on rocks, or an onrushing train).

sources.title: Frank Hurley OBE - The Australian Museum
sources.excerpt: In 1911 Hurley became official photographer to Douglas Mawson's first Australasian Antarctic Expedition. At the windiest place on Earth, he worked enthusiastically taking stills and moving images, and took part in a record-breaking sledging journey to the South Magnetic Pole.

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Hurley, James Francis (Frank)
sources.excerpt: Shackleton had forced Hurley to leave his glass negatives on board Endurance when they abandoned ship, however, before the ship broke up Hurley went back and retrieved some of his negatives. He was only able to save about 150 of 500 negatives as this was all he could fit in his storage tin.

sources.title: Freeze Frame (Scott Polar Research Institute) » Biography of Hurley, James Francis (Frank)
sources.excerpt: During the First World War, Hurley served as an official war photographer in France and in the Middle East, his colour slides are among the few colour images of the First World War. In both his polar and war photography Hurley used a process of combination printing, combining several negatives to produced one dramatic image.

photographers.bio_md: Frank Hurley (1885–1962) wurde in Sydney geboren, verließ die Schule ohne Abschluss und arbeitete in einem Stahlwerk [Q1]. Er brachte sich mit einer Kodak-Boxkamera das Fotografieren selbst bei und wurde bei einem Postkartenverlag für Qualität und Wagemut bekannt [Q2]. 1911 wurde er offizieller Fotograf von Douglas Mawsons Australasischer Antarktisexpedition [Q3]; auf Shackletons Endurance-Expedition rettete er nach dem Untergang des Schiffs etwa 150 von 500 Glasnegativen [Q4]. Im Ersten Weltkrieg war er offizieller Kriegsfotograf in Frankreich und im Nahen Osten; seine Farbdias gehören zu den wenigen Farbbildern dieses Krieges [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Hurley suchte das spektakuläre Bild und ging dafür Risiken ein, etwa vor brechenden Wellen oder einem heranrasenden Zug [Q2]. Sowohl in der Polar- als auch in der Kriegsfotografie kombinierte er mehrere Negative zu einem dramatischen Bild (Kombinationsdruck) [Q5].

photographers.name: Edward Burtynsky

portrait.credit: Christopher Michel / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Biography — Edward Burtynsky
sources.excerpt: Burtynsky was born in 1955 of Ukrainian heritage in St. Catharines, Ontario. He received his BAA in Photography/Media Studies from Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly Ryerson University) in 1982, and has since received both an Alumni Achievement Award (2004) and an Honorary Doctorate (2007) from his alma mater.

sources.title: Biography — Edward Burtynsky
sources.excerpt: Early exposure to the General Motors plant and watching ships go by in the Welland Canal in Burtynsky's hometown helped capture his imagination for the scale of human creation, and to formulate the development of his photographic work. His imagery explores the collective impact we as a species are having on the surface of the planet - an inspection of the human systems we've imposed onto natural landscapes.

sources.title: Biography — Edward Burtynsky
sources.excerpt: Edward Burtynsky is regarded as one of the world's most accomplished contemporary photographers. His remarkable photographic depictions of global industrial landscapes represent over 40 years of his dedication to bearing witness to the impact of human industry on the planet.

sources.title: DJI Creator Profile: Edward Burtynsky Uses Drones To Chronicle Our Anthropocene Age
sources.excerpt: For many of his works, Burtynsky uses a large format camera. He finds a vantage point he can climb to high above his subject, or uses a helicopter to get the right perspective.

sources.title: Edward Burtynsky Interview – A Photo Editor
sources.excerpt: I've always been interested in being able to position my camera at an optimal viewpoint in order to take a good picture. My response to a subject determines the appropriate distance, angle and time of year.

photographers.bio_md: Edward Burtynsky wurde 1955 in St. Catharines (Ontario) in einer ukrainischstämmigen Familie geboren und schloss 1982 ein Studium in Fotografie/Medien an der heutigen Toronto Metropolitan University ab [Q1]. Das GM-Werk und die Schiffe im Welland-Kanal seiner Heimatstadt weckten früh sein Gespür für den Maßstab menschlicher Schöpfungen [Q2]. Seit über 40 Jahren zeigt er industrielle Landschaften weltweit und bezeugt die Wirkung der Industrie auf den Planeten [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Burtynsky arbeitet oft mit der Großformatkamera und sucht einen hohen Standpunkt über dem Motiv – auf einer Erhöhung oder aus dem Hubschrauber [Q4]. Die Reaktion auf das Motiv bestimmt Distanz, Winkel und Jahreszeit; entscheidend ist der optimale Kamerastandpunkt [Q5].

photographers.name: Olaf Otto Becker

portrait.credit: Bild der Bio-Seite von olafottobecker.com (Fotograf nicht angegeben); © Olaf Otto Becker, nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Bio | olafottobecker.de
sources.excerpt: Born 1959 in Travemünde, by the Baltic Sea, Germany. From 1981 to 1986 I was in Augsburg, studying communciation design. Until 1988 I studied philosophy and political science in Munich.

sources.title: Bio | olafottobecker.de
sources.excerpt: My first book, Under the Nordic Light, features landscape photographies of Iceland and was nominated in the category of Best Book at the Recontres International de la Photographies Arles in 2006. For my book Broken Line, I traveled 4000 km in a small dinghy along the west coast of Greenland to document climate change with my 8 x 10 camera. Broken Line was awarded the 2007 German Photo Book Prize.

sources.title: Bio | olafottobecker.de
sources.excerpt: From 2008 till 2014 I worked on book titled Reading the Landscape, which discusses the worldwide deforestation of primary forests and the current rearrangement of our understanding of nature. In my work I combine my personal and artistic approach with documentary intention and socio-cultural questions.

sources.title: Alone with the icebergs | Signs of change: Olaf Otto Becker – GalleryViewer
sources.excerpt: He would sail along all the glaciers on Greenland's west coast, capture them with his large-format camera and record the GPS coordinates so that someone, 50 or 100 years in the future, could document the changes.

sources.title: Alone with the icebergs | Signs of change: Olaf Otto Becker – GalleryViewer
sources.excerpt: With the empty horizon and diffused light, the viewer has no point of reference - not for the time of day when Becker took the picture or the scale of the icebergs.

photographers.bio_md: Olaf Otto Becker wurde 1959 in Travemünde geboren, studierte 1981–1986 Kommunikationsdesign in Augsburg und bis 1988 Philosophie und Politikwissenschaft in München [Q1]. Sein erstes Buch „Under the Nordic Light“ über Island war 2006 in Arles nominiert; für „Broken Line“ fuhr er 4000 km im kleinen Schlauchboot an Grönlands Westküste entlang, um den Klimawandel zu dokumentieren, und erhielt dafür den Deutschen Fotobuchpreis 2007 [Q2]. 2008–2014 arbeitete er an „Reading the Landscape“ über die weltweite Abholzung von Urwäldern [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Becker fotografiert mit der 8×10-Zoll-Großformatkamera [Q2] und verbindet persönlichen künstlerischen Zugang mit dokumentarischer Absicht [Q3]. In Grönland notierte er GPS-Koordinaten jedes Standorts, damit spätere Fotografen die Veränderungen dokumentieren können [Q4]. Leerer Horizont und diffuses Licht nehmen dem Betrachter jeden Anhaltspunkt für Tageszeit und Größe der Eisberge [Q5].

photographers.name: Fay Godwin

sources.title: Fay Godwin · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Fay Godwin British, born Germany 1931, Berlin, Germany 2005, Hastings, England

sources.title: Fay Godwin - Imperial Health Charity
sources.excerpt: Born in Berlin, Germany, to a British diplomat and an American artist, Fay Godwin spent her childhood abroad. In 1966, she became interested in photography through capturing her young children. She was largely self-taught, mastering the techniques of developing and printing her own photographs.

sources.title: Fay Godwin | The Women's Art Collection, Murray Edwards College
sources.excerpt: Fay Godwin was a photographer known for her poetic black-and-white interpretations of the British landscape and portraits of prominent writers.

sources.title: Fay Godwin | The Women's Art Collection, Murray Edwards College
sources.excerpt: Godwin published her first landscape photography book, The Oldest Road , in 1975. She rose to prominence in the late 1980s with the exhibition and accompanying book Land (1985), becoming the first living photographer featured on ITV's South Bank Show in 1986. President of the Ramblers' Association (1987-90) and campaigner for open access to the countryside, an appreciation of the British landscape underpinned her environmental activism.

sources.title: Fay Godwin - Imperial Health Charity
sources.excerpt: In 1979, she collaborated with Poet Laureate Ted Hughes on Remains of Elmet . The book is a collection of poems by Ted Hughes with photographs by Fay Godwin.

photographers.bio_md: Fay Godwin wurde 1931 in Berlin geboren und starb 2005 in Hastings [Q1]. Als Tochter eines britischen Diplomaten und einer amerikanischen Künstlerin wuchs sie im Ausland auf; 1966 kam sie über Fotos ihrer kleinen Kinder zur Fotografie und war weitgehend Autodidaktin [Q2]. Bekannt wurde sie für poetische Schwarzweißbilder der britischen Landschaft und Porträts von Schriftstellern [Q3]. Nach ihrem ersten Landschaftsbuch „The Oldest Road“ (1975) gelang ihr mit „Land“ (1985) der Durchbruch; 1987–90 war sie Präsidentin der Ramblers' Association und setzte sich für freien Zugang zur Landschaft ein [Q4]. 1979 erschien „Remains of Elmet“ mit Gedichten von Ted Hughes [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Godwin entwickelte und vergrößerte ihre Bilder selbst [Q2]. Ihre Liebe zur britischen Landschaft war mit Wandern und Umweltengagement verbunden [Q4].

photographers.name: Laura Gilpin

portrait.credit: Fotograf unbekannt / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Laura Gilpin - Masterworks | Andrew Smith Gallery
sources.excerpt: Born in 1891 and raised in Colorado Springs, she began photographing in 1903 at the age of twelve and continued until her death in Santa Fe in 1979. As one of the few significant women landscape photographers in the history of photography, Gilpin photographed the American Southwest for more than sixty years, creating an extraordinary document of the land and its people.

sources.title: Laura Gilpin - Masterworks | Andrew Smith Gallery
sources.excerpt: In 1916, many years after taking up photography she moved to New York and enrolled in the Clarence H. White School where she studied photography under White, Paul Anderson, and Max Weber. Influenced by White, Gilpin strove to capture the lasting essence of a subject, rather than a fleeting or temporal image, and to record the emotion of a scene rather than its literal appearance.

sources.title: Laura Gilpin | Amon Carter Museum of American Art
sources.excerpt: Study with Clarence H. White led her to initially embrace a pictorialist style that emphasized beauty and artistic creation over photography's documentary qualities. But over time she developed a more straightforward photographic approach, becoming widely known for her extended documentation of the Southwestern landscape and the Diné (Navajo) people.

sources.title: Laura Gilpin - Masterworks | Andrew Smith Gallery
sources.excerpt: Gilpin had a life long passion for platinum prints with their wide tonal range, rich velvety blacks and archival stability. She used platinum papers and textured silver paper almost exclusively through the 1935.

sources.title: Laura Gilpin | Amon Carter Museum of American Art
sources.excerpt: In 1979 Gilpin bequeathed the Museum over 6,000 prints and 20,000 negatives as well as her personal library collection, and the Laura Gilpin Papers .

photographers.bio_md: Laura Gilpin wurde 1891 geboren, wuchs in Colorado Springs auf, fotografierte ab 1903 und starb 1979 in Santa Fe; über sechzig Jahre lang dokumentierte sie den amerikanischen Südwesten, Land und Menschen [Q1]. 1916 studierte sie in New York an der Clarence H. White School bei White, Paul Anderson und Max Weber [Q2]. Zunächst arbeitete sie piktorialistisch, entwickelte dann einen direkteren Stil und wurde für ihre lange Dokumentation der Landschaft des Südwestens und der Diné (Navajo) bekannt [Q3]. Ihren Nachlass von über 6.000 Abzügen und 20.000 Negativen vermachte sie dem Amon Carter Museum [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Unter Whites Einfluss suchte Gilpin das dauerhafte Wesen eines Motivs statt eines flüchtigen Moments und wollte die Stimmung einer Szene festhalten, nicht ihr bloßes Aussehen [Q2]. Sie liebte Platindrucke mit ihrem weiten Tonumfang und samtigen Schwarz [Q4].

photographers.name: Hiroshi Sugimoto

portrait.credit: team art in berlin / CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Biography — Hiroshi Sugimoto
sources.excerpt: 1948 Born in Tokyo, Japan 1970 Graduated from Saint Paul's University, Tokyo 1974 Graduated from Art Center College of Design, Los Angeles 1974 Moved to New York

sources.title: Hiroshi Sugimoto · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Known for his long-exposure photographic series of empty movie theaters and drive-ins, seascapes, museum dioramas, and waxworks, Hiroshi Sugimoto has been investigating the nature of time for nearly thirty years.

sources.title: Hiroshi Sugimoto · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Born in postwar Tokyo, Sugimoto's interest in art began at an early age. He had already been deeply influenced by Surrealist thinkers and writers such as André Breton and Marcel Duchamp when he moved to Los Angeles to study photography at the Art Center College of Design.

sources.title: Hiroshi Sugimoto · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: In the 1990s Sugimoto produced a series of intentionally blurry, large-format photographs of iconic works of 20th-century architecture, including the Empire State Building and Le Corbusier's chapel at Ronchamp. In these out-of-focus pictures, the buildings are at once immediately identifiable and barely recognizable, an effect that draws attention to the mechanics of memory and perception.

sources.title: Seascapes — Hiroshi Sugimoto
sources.excerpt: Mystery of mysteries, water and air are right there before us in the sea. Every time I view the sea, I feel a calming sense of security, as if visiting my ancestral home; I embark on a voyage of seeing.

photographers.bio_md: Hiroshi Sugimoto wurde 1948 in Tokio geboren, schloss 1970 an der Rikkyo (Saint Paul's) University ab und 1974 am Art Center College of Design in Los Angeles; im selben Jahr zog er nach New York [Q1]. Schon vor dem Studium war er stark von Surrealisten wie André Breton und Marcel Duchamp beeinflusst [Q3]. Bekannt ist er für Langzeitbelichtungs-Serien leerer Kinos und Autokinos, Seestücke, Museumsdioramen und Wachsfiguren, mit denen er seit Jahrzehnten das Wesen der Zeit untersucht [Q2]. In den 1990ern entstanden absichtlich unscharfe Großformataufnahmen ikonischer Architektur des 20. Jahrhunderts [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Sugimoto arbeitet mit sehr langen Belichtungen, um Zeit selbst sichtbar zu machen [Q2]. Die bewusste Unschärfe seiner Architekturbilder lenkt den Blick auf die Mechanik von Erinnerung und Wahrnehmung [Q4]. Seine Seestücke beschreibt er als „Reise des Sehens“ zu Wasser und Luft, den Grundlagen des Lebens [Q5].

photographers.name: Eve Arnold

portrait.credit: Profilbild der Magnum-Photos-Fotografenseite (Selbstporträt im Spiegel; Urheberangabe auf der Seite nicht genannt); © Eve Arnold / Magnum Photos, nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Eve Arnold • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: Eve Arnold was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1912 to Russian immigrant parents. She began photographing in 1946 while working at a photo-finishing plant in New York City. She then studied photography in 1948 with Alexei Brodovitch at the New School for Social Research in New York.

sources.title: Photojournalism pioneer Eve Arnold dies at 99 | CNN
sources.excerpt: It was her photos of African-American fashion shows in Harlem, New York, in the early 1950s that first caught the eye of Henri Cartier-Bresson and won her entry to Magnum, at that time a highly male-dominated environment. She became a full member in 1957.

sources.title: Photojournalism pioneer Eve Arnold dies at 99 | CNN
sources.excerpt: "Her intimate, sensitive and compassionate 10-year collaboration with Marilyn Monroe has cemented her as one of the most iconic portrait photographers of our time, but it is the long-term reportage stories that drove Arnold's curiosity and passion," Magnum said.

sources.title: Eve Arnold • Photographer Profile • Magnum Photos
sources.excerpt: "If a photographer cares about the people before the lens and is compassionate, much is given. It is the photographer, not the camera, that is the instrument." - Eve Arnold

sources.title: Photojournalism pioneer Eve Arnold dies at 99 | CNN
sources.excerpt: Eve Arnold died on January 4 in London at age 99.

photographers.bio_md: Eve Arnold wurde 1912 in Philadelphia als Tochter russischer Einwanderer geboren, begann 1946 in einem Fotolabor zu fotografieren und studierte 1948 bei Alexei Brodovitch an der New School in New York [Q1]. Ihre Bilder afroamerikanischer Modenschauen in Harlem fielen Henri Cartier-Bresson auf und brachten sie zu Magnum, wo sie 1957 Vollmitglied wurde [Q2]. Ihre zehnjährige Zusammenarbeit mit Marilyn Monroe machte sie zu einer der bekanntesten Porträtfotografinnen, angetrieben wurde sie aber von langen Reportagen [Q3]. Sie starb im Januar 2012 mit 99 Jahren in London [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Für Arnold war der Fotograf, nicht die Kamera, das Instrument: Wer sich um die Menschen vor dem Objektiv kümmert und mitfühlend ist, dem wird viel gegeben [Q4]. Ihre Porträts gelten als intim, einfühlsam und mitfühlend [Q3].

photographers.name: Eliot Porter

portrait.credit: [Eliot Porter shooting a 35mm camera], 1982, Fotograf unbekannt; Amon Carter Museum of American Art, P1990.59.155 (laut Museum: Public domain). Bildausschnitt der Museumsseite.

sources.title: Eliot Porter – Biography | Amon Carter Museum of American Art
sources.excerpt: Eliot Furness Porter was born in 1901 in the Chicago suburb of Winnetka, Illinois, the second of five children in an upper middle-class family.

sources.title: Eliot Porter: In the Realm of Nature (Getty Center Exhibitions)
sources.excerpt: Eliot Porter was trained as a chemical engineer and a medical doctor. He began his photography career in the 1930s, making black-and-white photographs in his spare time while working as a bacteriologist and teacher at Harvard University. Photographer Alfred Stieglitz gave Porter a solo exhibition at his New York art gallery in 1938.

sources.title: Eliot Porter – Biography | Amon Carter Museum of American Art
sources.excerpt: Although he had previously photographed in black and white, in 1939 Porter took up color to create more accurate photographs of birds. Soon he added other woodland subjects to his repertoire and became the first established artist-photographer to commit to exploring the natural world almost exclusively in color.

sources.title: Eliot Porter – Biography | Amon Carter Museum of American Art
sources.excerpt: But in 1962, he gained a major boost when the Sierra Club published In Wildness Is the Preservation of the World . That immensely popular book, which combines his evocative photographs of New England woods with excerpts from the writings of Henry David Thoreau, revolutionized photographic book publishing by setting new standards for color printing and proving the commercial viability of fine art photography books.

sources.title: Eliot Porter: In the Realm of Nature (Getty Center Exhibitions)
sources.excerpt: For the next three decades he struggled against the notion that color photography was unsuitable for artists because it was "too literal." Porter actually used the color process to make highly expressive prints by slightly increasing the brilliance, contrast, or saturation in the transparencies.

photographers.bio_md: Eliot Porter wurde 1901 in Winnetka bei Chicago geboren [Q1]. Er war ausgebildeter Chemieingenieur und Arzt und fotografierte in den 1930ern nebenbei schwarzweiß, während er in Harvard als Bakteriologe arbeitete; 1938 gab ihm Alfred Stieglitz eine Einzelausstellung [Q2]. 1939 wechselte er zur Farbe, zunächst für Vogelbilder, und wurde der erste etablierte Künstlerfotograf, der die Natur fast ausschließlich in Farbe erkundete [Q3]. 1962 veröffentlichte der Sierra Club „In Wildness Is the Preservation of the World“ mit Thoreau-Texten – ein Buch, das neue Maßstäbe im Farbdruck setzte [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Porter kämpfte gegen das Vorurteil, Farbe sei „zu wörtlich“ für Kunst, und machte sehr ausdrucksstarke Abzüge, indem er Brillanz, Kontrast oder Sättigung der Dias leicht anhob [Q5].

photographers.name: Nick Brandt

portrait.credit: Topangahomeboy / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Art in Dialogue: Artist Talk with Nick Brandt, Environmental Photographer | Lehigh University Art Galleries
sources.excerpt: About Nick Brandt Nick Brandt (born 1964) is an English photographer, whose work focuses on the rapidly disappearing natural world, as a result of environmental destruction, climate change and human actions. Raised in London, Brandt studied painting and then film at Saint Martin's School of Art.

sources.title: Inherit the Dust — Multimedia Art Museum, Moscow
sources.excerpt: Nick Brandt first visited Tanzania in 1995, while filming a clip for Jackson's "Earth Song", which is dedicated to protection of the environment. That trip radically changed Brandt's life: he fell in love with the natural world of Africa and decided to devote himself to photography.

sources.title: Art in Dialogue: Artist Talk with Nick Brandt, Environmental Photographer | Lehigh University Art Galleries
sources.excerpt: Brandt's ambitious photographic project, a trilogy of books memorializing the fast-disappearing natural grandeur of East Africa, was shot on medium-format black and white film without telephoto or zoom lenses. This body of work was a combination of epic panoramas of animals within dramatic landscapes and graphic, intimate portraits similar to studio portraiture of human subjects from the early 20th Century.

sources.title: Inherit the Dust — Multimedia Art Museum, Moscow
sources.excerpt: My aim is for the images to go beyond the animal documentary genre and reach the arena of fine art photography. To achieve this I eschew action shots and, most importantly, the use of a telephoto lens. Instead I move in close, often taking photos from a few feet away.

sources.title: Inherit the Dust — Multimedia Art Museum, Moscow
sources.excerpt: Previously unpublished portraits of wild animals were printed in large format, pasted on panels and installed in locations where these animals once roamed but have now been wiped out due to human greed and indifference. Nick Brandt then photographed the panels, combining urban landscapes and animal images in a single frame.

photographers.bio_md: Nick Brandt (geb. 1964) ist ein englischer Fotograf, der sich der schwindenden Natur widmet; er wuchs in London auf und studierte Malerei und Film an der Saint Martin's School of Art [Q1]. Als er 1995 in Tansania Michael Jacksons „Earth Song“ drehte, verliebte er sich in die Natur Afrikas und wandte sich der Fotografie zu [Q2]. Seine Trilogie über die verschwindende Größe Ostafrikas verbindet epische Tierpanoramen mit Porträts im Stil früher Atelierfotografie [Q3]. Für „Inherit the Dust“ stellte er großformatige Tierporträts auf Tafeln dort auf, wo die Tiere inzwischen verschwunden sind, und fotografierte sie in der Industrie- und Stadtlandschaft [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Brandt fotografierte auf Mittelformat-Schwarzweißfilm ohne Tele- oder Zoomobjektive [Q3]. Er verzichtet auf Actionbilder und geht nah heran, oft auf wenige Fuß, um Tierbilder in die Kunstfotografie zu heben [Q4].

photographers.name: Richard Misrach

portrait.credit: BurnAway / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Richard Misrach | Art21
sources.excerpt: Richard Misrach was born in 1949 in Los Angeles, California. A leading photographer of his generation, Misrach explores the collision of nature and culture through his large-format color photographs.

sources.title: Richard Misrach | Art21
sources.excerpt: Misrach began his career in Berkeley, California, in the early 1970s, photographing the anti-war protests happening throughout the city. His first major series of photographs, Telegraph 3 AM (1974), depicted the homeless population of Telegraph Avenue in Berkeley. Misrach realized that the work failed to meet his social-activist ambitions and instead turned his camera to the deserts of southern California, Nevada, and Arizona.

sources.title: Richard Misrach | Art21
sources.excerpt: His ongoing series, Desert Cantos , consists of groups of photographs that depict the ecological effects of human intervention in the desert landscape. A more recent chapter, Border Cantos , captures the pathos of the 2000-mile border between the U.S. and Mexico, including the border wall and the artifacts of migration-clothing, water barrels, ladders-left behind.

sources.title: Richard Misrach | Art21
sources.excerpt: Fascinated by the political and environmental transformation of the deserts of the American southwest, Misrach creates hauntingly beautiful photographs of arid landscapes that contrast the natural and man-made tragedies found there: floods, fires, nuclear-test sites, the U.S.-Mexico border wall, and the traces of migrants who make the perilous journey north.

sources.title: Richard Misrach · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: And along with the big camera, I took a small pocket camera, a 4 mega-pixel pocket camera. And that was just strictly to make notes about where I was, streets that were down- you know, street signs that were down, maybe places to go back and shoot. I never thought I would make serious pictures with that.

photographers.bio_md: Richard Misrach wurde 1949 in Los Angeles geboren und erforscht in großformatigen Farbfotografien den Zusammenstoß von Natur und Kultur [Q1]. Er begann Anfang der 1970er in Berkeley mit Bildern der Antikriegsproteste und der Serie „Telegraph 3 AM“ (1974) über Obdachlose, wandte sich dann aber den Wüsten Kaliforniens, Nevadas und Arizonas zu [Q2]. Seine fortlaufende Serie „Desert Cantos“ zeigt die ökologischen Folgen menschlicher Eingriffe in der Wüste; das Kapitel „Border Cantos“ widmet sich der Grenze zwischen USA und Mexiko [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Misrach macht eindringlich schöne Bilder trockener Landschaften, die zugleich natürliche und menschengemachte Katastrophen zeigen – Fluten, Brände, Atomtestgelände, die Grenzmauer [Q4]. Er arbeitet mit großer Kamera; nach Hurrikan Katrina entstanden aus einer kleinen Notizkamera unerwartet eigene, rohe Bilder [Q5].

photographers.name: Corinne Vionnet

portrait.credit: Foto: Monika Flückiger (laut Dateiname), Vortrag beim WEF 2013, via corinnevionnet.com; nur Ansicht/Link. Die Künstlerin ist klein rechts im Bild.

sources.title: About — Corinne Vionnet
sources.excerpt: Corinne Vionnet is a Franco-Swiss visual artist based in Switzerland. She is a pioneer in the exploration and re-purposing of web-based imagery. Her work includes extensive archival research, photographic image making, the appropriation of crowd-sourced material, and collage.

sources.title: Corinne Vionnet - Photo Opportunities | Kehrer Verlag
sources.excerpt: Conducting keyword searches of famed monuments in photo sharing web sites, Swiss /French artist Corinne Vionnet culled thousands of tourists' snapshots for her series Photo Opportunities. Weaving together numerous photographic perspectives and experiences, the artist builds her own impressionistic interpretations - ethereal structures which float gently in a dream-like haze of blue sky.

sources.title: A Hundred Tourist Photos In One : The Picture Show : NPR
sources.excerpt: Each image in Photo Opportunities is a collage of about 100 images aligned around a single point: Mao's face, the tip-top of Mount Fuji, the clock on the Big Ben tower.

sources.title: About — Corinne Vionnet
sources.excerpt: Her works led her to analyze the construction and maintenance of the social imagination and collective identity, as well as our behavior with images, with the act of taking of pictures as well as the content of these overflow of pictures.

sources.title: About — Corinne Vionnet
sources.excerpt: Her first monograph, Photo Opportunities , is published in 2011 (Kehrer Verlag, Germany).

photographers.bio_md: Corinne Vionnet ist eine französisch-schweizerische bildende Künstlerin mit Sitz in der Schweiz und eine Pionierin im Umgang mit Bildern aus dem Internet; ihre Arbeit umfasst Archivrecherche, eigene Fotografie, angeeignetes Crowd-Material und Collage [Q1]. Für die Serie „Photo Opportunities“ durchsuchte sie Foto-Plattformen nach berühmten Monumenten und sammelte Tausende Touristenschnappschüsse [Q2]; ihre erste Monografie mit diesem Titel erschien 2011 bei Kehrer [Q5]. Ihr Werk untersucht, wie soziale Vorstellungswelt und kollektive Identität entstehen, und unser Verhalten mit Bildern und beim Fotografieren [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Jedes Bild aus „Photo Opportunities“ ist eine Collage aus rund 100 Fotos, ausgerichtet an einem einzigen Punkt – etwa Maos Gesicht oder dem Gipfel des Fuji [Q3]. So entstehen impressionistische, ätherische Gebilde, die in einem traumartigen blauen Dunst schweben [Q2].

photographers.name: Penelope Umbrico

portrait.credit: Photo: courtesy the artist (SFMOMA-Künstlerseite); nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Penelope Umbrico · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Penelope Umbrico American 1957, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

sources.title: Penelope Umbrico Interview – A Photo Editor
sources.excerpt: Well, I moved to the states in '86. But before that I went to Ontario College of Art, as it was called when I was there. My major was Experimental Art – which I guess was the equivalent of new media today

sources.title: Penelope Umbrico Interview – A Photo Editor
sources.excerpt: Not seriously until I was doing my MFA in Painting at SVA. The earliest photographs were really looking at consumer culture, moving through it in a virtual way. I think all of the photographs that I've made deal with 'virtually' occupying another space.

sources.title: No Two Sunsets are Alike: Reenvisioning Umbrico's Suns… Nine Years Later · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: When Umbrico conceived the work in 2006, Flickr was becoming a popular photo sharing site, and she was intrigued by the number of people posting nearly the exact same picture: "sunset" was the most tagged word, with approximately 500,000 hits in 2006 (there have already been more than 35 million in 2018). Umbrico downloaded thousands of sunset images from Flickr and cropped 2,500 of them to focus on the sun.

sources.title: No Two Sunsets are Alike: Reenvisioning Umbrico's Suns… Nine Years Later · SFMOMA
sources.excerpt: Each time the work is shown in a gallery or acquired by another museum, the title is changed to reflect the number of sunsets on Flickr on that given day.

photographers.bio_md: Penelope Umbrico wurde 1957 in Philadelphia geboren [Q1]. Sie studierte am Ontario College of Art „Experimental Art“, zog 1986 in die USA [Q2] und begann ernsthaft zu fotografieren, als sie an der School of Visual Arts ihren MFA in Malerei machte; schon die ersten Bilder befassten sich mit Konsumkultur [Q3]. 2006 entwarf sie „Suns (from Sunsets) from Flickr“: Sie lud Tausende Sonnenuntergangsbilder von Flickr herunter und beschnitt 2.500 davon auf die Sonne [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Umbrico arbeitet mit vorhandenen Bildern aus dem Netz statt mit eigenen Aufnahmen auf der Straße; ihre Fotos handeln davon, einen anderen Raum „virtuell“ zu bewohnen [Q3]. Ausgangspunkt der „Suns“ war die Beobachtung, dass sehr viele Menschen fast dasselbe Bild posten [Q4]; der Werktitel ändert sich mit jeder Ausstellung nach der aktuellen Zahl der Sonnenuntergänge auf Flickr [Q5].

photographers.name: Christopher Burkett

portrait.credit: Bild der About-Seite von christopherburkett.com (Fotograf nicht angegeben); nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: About - Christopher Burkett | Handmade Cibachromes
sources.excerpt: Christopher Burkett was born in 1951 and grew up in Oregon. In 1975, while he was a brother in a Christian order, he became interested in photography as a means of expressing the grace, light and beauty he saw present in the world of nature.

sources.title: About - Christopher Burkett | Handmade Cibachromes
sources.excerpt: In 1979, Burkett left the brotherhood to pursue photography and married his wife, Ruth. He learned the offset printing process and ran large four-color printing presses and later laser drum scanners to making detailed color separations. Years of experience in the printing trade helped him develop his fine discernment of color and a deep understanding and mastery of color and tone reproduction.

sources.title: About - Christopher Burkett | Handmade Cibachromes
sources.excerpt: Burkett became a recognized national expert in printing Cibachrome (Ilfochrome Classic Deluxe) by virtue of his use of sophisticated and unique contrast and color correction masking techniques. His refined printing skills create exceptional prints with luminosity, depth and life.

sources.title: A Sense of Real Life - Western Art & Architecture
sources.excerpt: In the secular art world, it may seem unusual to learn that an artist who's been described as "the Ansel Adams of color photography" explains his artistic ethos as a way to reveal the "gift of God's grace to share with others." But as one of the last few photographers still using an 8-by-10-inch view camera and Cibachrome paper, Burkett's reverence for the transcendent makes perfect sense.

sources.title: A Sense of Real Life - Western Art & Architecture
sources.excerpt: Burkett acknowledges that while in the field taking exposures, he has a sense of how the scene will record and can visualize the eventual final print.

photographers.bio_md: Christopher Burkett wurde 1951 geboren und wuchs in Oregon auf; 1975, als Bruder in einem christlichen Orden, begann er zu fotografieren, um Gnade, Licht und Schönheit der Natur auszudrücken [Q1]. 1979 verließ er den Orden, heiratete und lernte im Offsetdruck und an Trommelscannern, was ihm ein feines Gespür für Farbe und Tonwiedergabe gab [Q2]. Er wurde als „Ansel Adams der Farbfotografie“ bezeichnet und gehört zu den letzten, die mit 8×10-Zoll-Fachkamera und Cibachrome arbeiten [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Burkett ist ein anerkannter Experte für Cibachrome-Abzüge und arbeitet mit aufwendigen Kontrast- und Farbkorrekturmasken für leuchtende, tiefe Prints [Q3]. Schon bei der Aufnahme visualisiert er, wie die Szene auf dem Film erscheint und wie der fertige Abzug aussehen wird [Q5].

photographers.name: Bruce Barnbaum

sources.title: About | Bruce Barnbaum
sources.excerpt: Bruce Barnbaum of Granite Falls gained Bachelor's and Master's degrees in mathematics from UCLA, then, after three years as a math analyst and computer programmer, abruptly turned to his hobby of photography as his life's work in 1970.

sources.title: About | Bruce Barnbaum
sources.excerpt: Starting in 1980 Bruce opened up photography of the slit canyons to the world for the first time. These remarkable wonders of nature had not been photographed prior to his discovery of them. In the canyons and elsewhere, Bruce works in both black and white and color, producing his b&w through traditional means (i.e., film and darkroom), and his color work digitally.

sources.title: About | Bruce Barnbaum
sources.excerpt: Visually he emphasizes the best of humanity and nature, sometimes with bold realism, often with degrees of abstraction to heighten the mystery. He understands light and relationships of forms to an extent rarely found, and combines these understandings to an extraordinarily wide range of subject matter. His photographs often contain ambiguities concerning either the size of the scene photographed and/or its orientation, forcing the viewer to pause and think, and to become part of the creative process.

sources.title: About | Bruce Barnbaum
sources.excerpt: The Art of Photography, A Personal Approach to Artistic Expression, his widely acclaimed textbook, has sold well over 100,000 copies in printed editions.

sources.title: Essay | Bruce Barnbaum
sources.excerpt: Having started using digital after nearly 40 years of traditional 4x5" film camera usage where I learned to carefully compose each image before exposing a negative, I find it hard to make an exposure - a so-called digital "capture" - without doing at least an initial quick assessment of some basic compositional elements within the scene...and also give thought to the quality of light before pressing the shutter.

photographers.bio_md: Bruce Barnbaum studierte Mathematik an der UCLA (Bachelor und Master), arbeitete drei Jahre als Analyst und Programmierer und machte 1970 sein Hobby Fotografie zum Lebenswerk [Q1]. Ab 1980 machte er die Slot Canyons als Erster fotografisch bekannt [Q2]. Sein Lehrbuch „The Art of Photography“ verkaufte sich über 100.000-mal [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Barnbaum fotografiert Schwarzweiß traditionell auf Film mit Dunkelkammer und Farbe digital [Q2]. Er betont Licht und Formbeziehungen, oft mit Abstraktion; Größe oder Ausrichtung der Szene bleiben bewusst mehrdeutig, damit der Betrachter innehält [Q3]. Nach fast 40 Jahren 4×5-Zoll-Film komponiert er jedes Bild sorgfältig und prüft vor dem Auslösen Bildelemente und Lichtqualität [Q5].

photographers.name: Michael Kenna

portrait.credit: © Matteo Colla / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Michael Kenna – Resume
sources.excerpt: Born 1953 in Widnes, Lancashire, England Currently lives in Seattle, Washington, USA 1973-76, London College of Printing, London, England. 1972-73, Banbury School of Art, Banbury, Oxfordshire, England

sources.title: Michael Kenna - Overview | Print Sales Gallery | The Photographers' Gallery
sources.excerpt: Kenna has lived in the United States since his mid-twenties but was born in England (1953) where he studied at a seminary school as a boy, intending to become a priest. His early encounters with ritual and faith left a lasting appreciation for mystery, doubt and the unseen.

sources.title: Michael Kenna - Overview | Print Sales Gallery | The Photographers' Gallery
sources.excerpt: Over five decades, Kenna has developed a distinctive visual language - a dialogue between dramatic chiaroscuro and the quiet minimalism of Japan, where he has regularly photographed since 1987. Many of Kenna's images are made at dawn or at night, often using long exposures, some lasting up to ten hours. Primarily working with a 120 mm analogue camera and printing each image by hand in the darkroom, he creates luminous silver gelatin prints

sources.title: photo-eye | BLOG: Michael Kenna: New Images from Japan
sources.excerpt: "I often think of my work as visual haiku. It is an attempt to evoke and suggest through as few elements as possible rather than to describe with tremendous detail."

sources.title: photo-eye | BLOG: Michael Kenna: New Images from Japan
sources.excerpt: "I gravitate towards places where humans have been and are no more, to the edge of man's influence, where the elements are taking over or covering man's traces."

photographers.bio_md: Michael Kenna wurde 1953 in Widnes (Lancashire) geboren, studierte an der Banbury School of Art und am London College of Printing und lebt in Seattle [Q1]. Als Junge besuchte er ein Priesterseminar; daraus blieb ihm ein Sinn für Geheimnis, Zweifel und das Unsichtbare [Q2]. Seine Bildsprache verbindet dramatisches Helldunkel mit der stillen Reduktion Japans, wo er seit 1987 regelmäßig fotografiert [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Kenna fotografiert oft im Morgengrauen oder nachts mit Langzeitbelichtungen bis zu zehn Stunden, meist mit einer analogen Mittelformatkamera, und vergrößert jedes Bild von Hand [Q3]. Er versteht seine Bilder als „visuelle Haiku“: andeuten mit möglichst wenigen Elementen statt detailreich beschreiben [Q4]. Ihn ziehen Orte an, an denen Menschen waren und nicht mehr sind [Q5].

photographers.name: Charlie Waite

portrait.credit: Garry Knight at https://www.flickr.com/photos/garryknight/ / CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: About — Charlie Waite
sources.excerpt: He was born in 1949 and worked as an actor in British theatre and television for the first ten years of his professional life. Throughout this period, he became fascinated by theatrical lighting and design. Gradually, the landscape and the way it can be revealed to us through light and shade stole him away from the acting profession.

sources.title: About — Charlie Waite
sources.excerpt: His style is unique in that his photographs convey a spiritual quality of serenity and calm. He has established a worldwide reputation for his particular approach to his work.

sources.title: About — Charlie Waite
sources.excerpt: Charlie is the owner and founder of Light and Land, the UK's leading photographic workshop and tour company.

sources.title: About — Charlie Waite
sources.excerpt: In 2007, Charlie launched the UK Landscape Photographer of the Year, an international photography competition to find the UK's 'Landscape Photographer of the Year', which ties in perfectly with his desire to share his passion and appreciation of the beauty of our surroundings through photography.

sources.title: Silent Exchange — Charlie Waite
sources.excerpt: Each reflects a moment when the elements within the frame seemed to settle into their own sense of balance - a stillness discovered through looking, composing and waiting.

photographers.bio_md: Charlie Waite wurde 1949 geboren und arbeitete die ersten zehn Berufsjahre als Schauspieler in britischem Theater und Fernsehen; dabei faszinierten ihn Bühnenlicht und Bühnenbild, bis ihn die Landschaft und ihr Spiel von Licht und Schatten vom Schauspiel weglockten [Q1]. Er gründete Light and Land, Großbritanniens führenden Anbieter für Fotoworkshops und -reisen [Q3], und rief 2007 den Wettbewerb „UK Landscape Photographer of the Year“ ins Leben [Q4].
photographers.method_md: Waites Bilder vermitteln eine fast spirituelle Ruhe und Gelassenheit [Q2]. Er sucht den Moment, in dem sich die Elemente im Bild in ein eigenes Gleichgewicht fügen – eine Stille, gefunden durch Schauen, Komponieren und Warten [Q5].

photographers.name: Joe Cornish

portrait.credit: Bild der Startseite von joecornish.co.uk (Dateiname „Joe-desert“, Fotograf nicht angegeben); zeigt ihn klein in einer Dünenlandschaft; nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Background — Joe Cornish
sources.excerpt: Joe began his photographic career in 1980 after completing a Bachelor of Fine Arts at Reading University. He spent the next four years assisting photographers in Washington DC and London, on location and in the studio. From the mid-1980s, Joe worked freelance in London doing portraits, studio and commercial work, and tourist imagery.

sources.title: Background — Joe Cornish
sources.excerpt: Joe's goals were completely re-set after working as expedition photographer for Raleigh International in Alaska during the summer of 1991. That experience inspired his belief in the importance of preserving wilderness and wild land globally. Landscape photography soon became his focus, at around the same time as Joe moved to North Yorkshire in 1993.

sources.title: Joe Cornish | Landscape Photographer
sources.excerpt: He works in the eye-witness tradition, creating images which are faithful to the subject. He is recognised for his grand landscapes of mountains, coast, moorland and woodland, particularly in the UK.

sources.title: Background — Joe Cornish
sources.excerpt: Having worked consistently on landscape in the north of England, Scotland and beyond for several years, Joe was asked by Eddie Ephraums, the commissioning editor at Aurum/Argentum, to write a book on his photographic practice, which led to the publication of First Light in 2003.

sources.title: Background — Joe Cornish
sources.excerpt: Joe prints all his own work and has invested significant time in honing his printing process to ensure accurate reproduction of digital originals. His prints are almost exclusively on matt fine-art papers, notably Fotospeed Platinum Cotton.

photographers.bio_md: Joe Cornish begann seine Laufbahn 1980 nach einem Kunststudium (BFA) an der University of Reading, assistierte vier Jahre in Washington und London und arbeitete ab Mitte der 1980er frei für Porträt-, Studio-, Werbe- und Tourismusaufträge [Q1]. Ein Einsatz als Expeditionsfotograf in Alaska 1991 richtete seine Ziele neu aus; mit dem Umzug nach North Yorkshire 1993 wurde die Landschaft sein Schwerpunkt [Q2]. 2003 erschien „First Light“ über seine fotografische Praxis [Q4]. Bekannt ist er für große Landschaften aus Bergen, Küsten, Mooren und Wäldern, vor allem in Großbritannien [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Cornish arbeitet in der Tradition des Augenzeugen und will dem Motiv treu bleiben [Q3]. Er druckt alle Bilder selbst, fast ausschließlich auf matten Fine-Art-Papieren [Q5].

photographers.name: Hans Strand

portrait.credit: Offizielles Pressebild (Dateiname „HansStrandOfficialPressImage“), hansstrand.se; Copyright-Vermerk im Bild, Fotograf nicht lesbar; nur Ansicht/Link

sources.title: Hans Strand Photography
sources.excerpt: Hans Strand, born in 1955 in Marmaverken, Sweden. In 1990, after a nine-year career in mechanical engineering he decided to devote his life to landscape photography.

sources.title: Interview with Hans Strand | Iceland Photo Tours
sources.excerpt: At first, the inspiration came from North American landscape photographers like Ansel Adams and David Muench and later from all kinds of documentary photographers like Henri Cartier Bresson, Sebastiao Salgado, Edward Burtynsky etc.

sources.title: Hans Strand Photography
sources.excerpt: The internationally awarded landscape photography is seldom a portrait of a place, but an expression of forces that create and mold a landscape. Hispictures, frozen in a static frame, still tell a story of movement, time and evolution. Lately his photography has also taken a course away from the untouched and wild nature and focused more on people´s influences on ecosystems.

sources.title: Hans Strand Photography
sources.excerpt: He has won thirteen international awards, including the Hasselblad Master Award in 2008. He has published seven books, often with themes relating to the environment and peoples relations to nature and landscapes.

sources.title: Hans Strand Photography
sources.excerpt: It covers both images from ground level and from above. Results of thousands of kilometers of criss-crossing the land by 4WD and more than 130 hours photographing from the air from Cessnas and helicopters.

photographers.bio_md: Hans Strand wurde 1955 in Marmaverken (Schweden) geboren und widmete sich 1990, nach neun Jahren als Maschinenbauingenieur, ganz der Landschaftsfotografie [Q1]. Anregung fand er zuerst bei nordamerikanischen Landschaftsfotografen wie Ansel Adams und David Muench, später bei Dokumentarfotografen wie Cartier-Bresson, Salgado und Burtynsky [Q2]. Er gewann dreizehn internationale Preise, darunter 2008 den Hasselblad Masters Award, und veröffentlichte sieben Bücher [Q4]. Zuletzt rückte der Einfluss des Menschen auf Ökosysteme stärker in seinen Blick [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Strands Bilder sind selten Porträts eines Ortes, sondern Ausdruck der Kräfte, die eine Landschaft formen – Bewegung, Zeit und Entwicklung im starren Bildrahmen [Q3]. Für sein Island-Buch fotografierte er vom Boden und über 130 Stunden aus Cessnas und Hubschraubern [Q5].

photographers.name: Jungjin Lee

portrait.credit: Jindřich Nosek (NoJin) / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.title: Jungjin Lee | Bellas Artes Gallery
sources.excerpt: Born in Korea in 1961, Lee mastered calligraphy as a child and studied ceramics at Hong - Ik University in Seoul. She lived in New York City from 1988 - 1996 where she absorbed the contemporary art scene and received a master's degree in photography from New York University. During her years as a graduate student, she worked as an assistant for photographer/filmmaker Robert Frank.

sources.title: Jungjin Lee | Bellas Artes Gallery
sources.excerpt: She does not mechanically reproduce multiples, but creates each work by hand. She brushes liquid emulsion onto large sheets of handmade rice and mulberry papers. Her brushstrokes sweep across the soft texture of the paper and capture the photographic image, revealing a painters sensibility in a gestural dance.

sources.title: Jungjin Lee | Bellas Artes Gallery
sources.excerpt: Out in the field, in the forest, or in the village, I am ready to press the shutter release when the scenery stirs my emotions and imagination.

sources.title: Jungjin Lee | Bellas Artes Gallery
sources.excerpt: The series was made in a wide panoramic format on gelatin silver coated Korean Hanji paper.

sources.title: Jungjin Lee | Bellas Artes Gallery
sources.excerpt: In the US, her work is included in the collections of The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Whitney Museum, Los Angeles County Museum of Art, Museum of Fine Arts in Houston, and New Mexico Museum of Art.

photographers.bio_md: Jungjin Lee wurde 1961 in Korea geboren, beherrschte schon als Kind die Kalligrafie und studierte Keramik an der Hongik-Universität in Seoul; 1988–1996 lebte sie in New York, machte an der New York University einen Master in Fotografie und assistierte Robert Frank [Q1]. Ihre Arbeiten befinden sich u. a. im Metropolitan Museum of Art, im Whitney Museum und im LACMA [Q5].
photographers.method_md: Lee druckt jedes Bild von Hand: Sie streicht flüssige Fotoemulsion mit dem Pinsel auf große Bögen handgeschöpften Reis- und Maulbeerpapiers [Q2]. Die Serie „Wind“ entstand im breiten Panoramaformat auf koreanischem Hanji-Papier [Q4]. Sie löst aus, wenn eine Landschaft ihre Gefühle und Vorstellungskraft bewegt [Q3].

photographers.name: Awoiska van der Molen

sources.title: Awoiska van der Molen - Huis Marseille, Museum voor Fotografie
sources.excerpt: In the summer of 2024 Huis Marseille will exhibit new work by the Dutch photographer Awoiska van der Molen (b. 1972 in Groningen). Critically acclaimed for her psychological landscape images, Awoiska van der Molen started out by photographing urban environments in 2003, shortly after graduating from art school.

sources.title: Biography | Awoiska van der Molen
sources.excerpt: She studied Architecture & Design before pursuing photography at Minerva Art Academy in Groningen and Hunter College, City University of New York. In 2003, she completed her MFA in Photography at St. Joost Academy in Breda, Netherlands.

sources.title: Biography | Awoiska van der Molen
sources.excerpt: Awoiska van der Molen is known for her monochrome analogue landscape images. Her work stems from an interest in the intangible, psychological qualities of her subjects.

sources.title: Awoiska van der Molen - Huis Marseille, Museum voor Fotografie
sources.excerpt: Her photographs demand slowness. Slowness during the creation of the image. Slowness in its materialisation. Slowness in viewing the results. The darkroom is where Van der Molen allows her images to slowly appear again.

sources.title: Awoiska van der Molen - Huis Marseille, Museum voor Fotografie
sources.excerpt: During solitary walks in the remote wilderness, Van der Molen attempts to penetrate the essence of a place.

photographers.bio_md: Awoiska van der Molen wurde 1972 in Groningen geboren und fotografierte nach dem Kunststudium ab 2003 zunächst städtische Umgebungen; bekannt wurde sie mit psychologisch aufgeladenen Landschaftsbildern [Q1]. Sie studierte Architektur und Design, dann Fotografie an der Minerva-Akademie in Groningen und am Hunter College in New York und schloss 2003 ihren MFA an der St. Joost Academy in Breda ab [Q2]. Ihr Werk besteht aus monochromen, analogen Landschaften und gilt den nicht greifbaren, psychologischen Qualitäten der Motive [Q3].
photographers.method_md: Auf einsamen Wanderungen in abgelegener Wildnis versucht van der Molen, zum Wesen eines Ortes vorzudringen [Q5]. Ihre Bilder verlangen Langsamkeit – beim Fotografieren, in der Dunkelkammer, beim Betrachten [Q4].
